### Main Process of Maintenance Operation

The maintenance operation is divided into the following three main processes:

1. Diagnosis;
2. Removal installation, replacement, disassembly assembly, inspection and adjustment;
3. Carry out final inspection

For the sake of concise description, and grasping the point, the following procedures are omitted from all maintenance operation descriptions in this manual, but these procedures must be carried out:

1. Use a jack or lift to jack or lift the vehicle; 2. Clean all the removed parts; 3. Visual inspection must be carried out before and after the work is carried out; 4. Conduct static test or road test on the vehicle after completion of the operation, and restore and clean the tools, equipment and stations.

### Contents

This manual is divided into six categories according to the functional aspects: overview, powertrain, chassis, body, interior and exterior trim and electrical. The previous level directory contains several next level directories.

In addition to the "overview" primary directory, each primary directory contains several secondary directories of the larger system or assembly associated with it; Each secondary directory contains multiple tertiary directories of subsystems or assembly associated with it; Each three-level catalog contains a variety of content classification catalogs according to actual needs, such as: precautions, system description, specifications, maintenance procedures (including disassembly and assembly, replacement, disassembly, detection, calibration, etc.).

### Safety and protection Notes

Many operations of vehicle maintenance and repair have potential physical injury or health hazards. Battery SafetySome of the hazardous operations and associated materials and equipment are listed in These hazards must be avoided and precautions must be followed.

Battery SafetyIt is not exhaustive, so all instructions of operation and procedures and the handling of materials must be carried out with health and safety.

Before using any product, consult the information for the product material safety provided by the manufacturer or supplier.

### Emergency Handling First Aid

The workshop must be staffed with first aid training.

Some examples of immediate action to be taken in case of emergency are given below:

If foreign objects splash into the eyes, carefully clean them with clean water for at least 10 min.

Skin contaminated with the material must be washed with soap and water.

If the body is burned by some substances, it must be washed with cold water immediately to cool down.

If one inhales fumes, he must immediately be moved to a place with fresh air and his physical condition is observed. If the situation still does not be improved, the patient must be taken to hospital immediately.

If person accidentally swallows the liquid, the information contained in the container or label must be provided to the doctor for consultation. Do not attempt vomiting on your own unless otherwise indicated on the label. In case of accidental electric shock, turn off the power supply and organize rescue for the sake of your safety.

Emergency Definition

Definition: An emergency refers to an abnormal fault that occurs suddenly during the normal operation of the vehicle, with no predictability and preparation in advance.

Category:

Common faults that do not affect the passengers and drivers and property safety. Serious faults affecting the passengers and drivers and property safety.

Emergency response principles:

Handling of common faults: For common
faults, you can go to the service station for normal vehicle maintenance.
Handling of serious faults: The handling of serious faults is based on the principle of "Life First", that is, in any emergency, the safety of passengers and drivers will be guaranteed first.

### Collision Handling

Vehicle power battery leakage:

1. Set the vehicle to OFF and keep it stationary for 5min.
2. Power off the low voltage electrical system. See
3. Disconnect the power maintenance switch (if equipped);
4. Disconnect the positive and negative busbars of the power battery;
5. Insulate and seal the positive and negative busbar connectors of the power battery and the harness connectors to prevent short circuits and foreign objects.

6. In case of a small amount of electrolyte leakage, keep away from the fire source, absorb the electrolyte with an absorbent pad and place it in a closed container, or dispose it by incineration; In case of a large number of leaks, collect them uniformly and treat them as hazardous chemicals. Calcium gluconate solution can be added for treatment to reduce the generation of harmful gas HF.

7. Drag the vehicle to the service store for power battery removal, and store the power battery safely after removal.

8. For the above steps, see Safe Maintenanceand Battery Safetyconduct the whole process monitoring and risk identification and treatment.

Operators in steps 3, 4, and 5, and e must wear insulating shoes, insulating gloves and insulating pads.

Operators in steps 6 and 7 must wear insulating shoes, acid and alkali resistant gloves and protective goggles.

Deformation of power battery:

1. Set the vehicle to OFF and keep it stationary for 5min.
2. Power off the low voltage electrical system. See
3. Disconnect the maintenance switch (if equipped).
4. Disconnect the positive and negative busbars of the power battery;
5. Use insulating tape to insulate and seal the positive and negative busbar connectors of the power battery and the harness connectors to prevent short circuits and foreign objects.
6. Drag the vehicle to the service store for power battery removal, and store the power battery safely after removal.
7. Disconnect each module of the power battery, if seriously deformed, for storage;
8. For the above steps, see Safe Maintenanceand Battery Safetyconduct the whole process monitoring and risk identification and treatment. Operators in steps 3, 4, 5, 6, and 7, and e must wear insulating shoes, insulating gloves and insulating pads.

Damaged vehicle sealing:

1. When waiting for maintenance, move the vehicle to a place without water ingress and corrosion risk for safe storage; 2. If the vehicle cannot be moved to a place without water ingress and corrosion risk for safe storage, it is necessary to cover it with a waterproof cover to avoid the risk of water ingress and corrosion.

### Smoke and Fire

Fire response plan

1. Use non-water-based fire extinguishers and fire-fighting sand to extinguish fires in nonpower battery parts and when the fire is small; 2. In the case that the above methods cannot realize the fire fighting, a large amount of water can be used to soak the vehicle; 3. After the fire in the power battery is put out, the power battery must be continuously cleaned with water for 30 min.

### ? Reminder:

In a fire, irritating toxic gases will be generated due to combustion or thermal decomposition reaction. In any closed area, firefighters must wear full protective equipment including positive pressure selfcontained breathing apparatus;

Emergency Treatment of Personnel Injury

Determination of electrolyte leakage of power battery:

1. In case of a large amount of electrolyte leakage, it is visible by naked eyes;
2. In case of a small amount of electrolyte leakage, such areas will be wet or have milky white spots;
3. Pungent smell means there is electrolyte leakage;

Emergency treatment method for exposure to electrolyte:

Under normal circumstances, when some human body parts are accidentally exposed to the leaked electrolyte, rinse the body
parts with plenty of water for 10\~15 min
immediately. If there is pain, apply 2.5%
calcium gluconate ointment to the pain areas or soak such areas in 2\~2.5% calcium
gluconate solution to relieve pain. If no
improvement or discomfort occurs, seek
medical advice immediately.
In case of eye contact, rinse eyes with fresh water for at least 15 min. If there is still
a pain feeling, please seek medical advice immediately.
In case of skin contact, remove contaminated clothing, wipe contaminants with a clean cloth immediately, and then rinse the contaminated areas thoroughly with soap and water. If
there is still a pain feeling, please seek
medical advice immediately.
In case of respiratory tract contact, move to a fresh air place. If you still breathe

hard or feel unwell, please seek medical advice immediately. In case of apnea, take cardiopulmonary resuscitation measures and seek medical advice immediately.

Emergency treatment method for electric
shock:
1. Turn off the power immediately if you can ensure your own safety.
2. Take insulation protection measures for yourself and others, and separate electric shock personnel from power supply.
3. To conduct emergency medical assistance on the scene, after the person who gets an electric shock is separated from the power supply, if he/she is conscious, let he/she rest quietly; in case of severe burns, send he/she to a hospital for treatment. If the person is unconscious and still has heartbeat and breathing, make the person lie on the back, and unbutton the clothes to facilitate breathing; ensure the surrounding air circulated, closely observe him/her, and see a doctor immediately for treatment or send he/she to a hospital for examination and treatment. If the electrocuted person has stopped breathing and the heart has stopped beating but has not died, defibrillators (if any) must be used immediately or cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) must be performed. The operation of cardiopulmonary resuscitation is as follows: a. Lay the electrocuted person on his back on a board or hard ground. b. Unbutton the neckline and trouser belt, and make his/her head tilt back as far as possible with nostrils facing the sky, so that the base of his/her tongue will not block the airway. c. Then open his mouth by hand to clean the foreign matters in the mouth and make the airway unblocked. d. Hold up his/her jaw with one hand, pinch his/her nose with the other hand, and give artificial respiration for about 2 s to expand the chest of the rescued person; then release his/her mouth and nose to let his/her chest compress naturally for exhalation about 3s.

### ® Reminder:

e. Repeat this procedure, with air blew about 12 times per minute.

f. If the mouth of the person who gets an electric shock can't be opened, give mouth-to-nose artificial respiration instead. At this time, larger blowing pressure is required and the air blowing time must be slightly longer, so as to facilitate the air to enter the lungs. g. If the person who gets an electric shock is a child, blow a small amount of air to avoid damaging his/her lungs. 4. Chest compressions must be performed at the same time of artificial respiration, about 100 compressions per minute with a compression depth of 5 cm.

### Common Sense of Safety Airbag

It is highly flammable and explosive, and strictly abides by the prohibition of fireworks.

The interior has a gas generator with a highenergy propellant that is normally completely sealed in the generator. Do not try to open it; otherwise, explosion may occur. When the propellant is ignited, it is completely consumed during the reaction and can produce high temperature gases (up to 2500 C). If the gas generator is broken, wear adequate protective clothing (e.g. protective clothing, protective gloves and goggles) to handle the spillage.

Used airbag must be packed in plastic bags and disposed of according to local regulations. If the human body is in direct contact with the gas generator, wash it thoroughly with clean water and seek medical advice according to severity.

Precautions for airbag operation:

Store the component in an upright position. Keep the component dry.
When the component is handled, the cover side must face the opposite side of the body. Place the protective cover of the component upward.
Carefully inspect the component for damage. Stand by the side of the component when connecting the airbag.
Ensure that all equipment is calibrated and maintained.
Always wash your hands after handling the triggered airbag.

Prohibited items of airbag operation:

Do not store it with highly flammable
materials.
Storage temperature: no more than 80° C Do not store it upside down.
Do not attempt to open the shell.
Do not expose it to open flame or heat
source.
Do not place anything on the surface
covering.
Do not use damaged airbag.
Do not touch the gas generator on fire for at least 10 min.
Do not use any electronic detectors on its harness.

### Refrigerant

It is highly flammable and explosive, and strictly abides by the prohibition of fireworks.

Direct skin contact may cause frostbite.

The instructions provided by the manufacturer must be followed. Wear suitable protective gloves and goggles when handling.

If refrigerant comes into direct contact with skin or eyes, rinse contaminated area immediately with clean water. In case of eye contact, it can also be cleaned with a suitable cleaning solution, and must not be wiped. Seek medical advice if you feel unwell.

Prohibited items of refrigerant operation:

Refrigerant bottle must not be exposed to the sun, or placed in a heat source.
Do not place the refrigerant bottle upright, and the valve must be downward during
filling.
Do not refrigerate the refrigerant bottle.
Do not drop the refrigerant bottle.
Do not discharge the refrigerant into the air. Never mix different refrigerant, such as R12 (Freon) and R134 a.

Precautions for marking, packaging, transportation and storage of refrigerant:

The refrigerant container must be provided with firm and clear marks, including: product name, trademark, production unit, address of production unit, net content, batch number, product grade, standard number and the "sun proof" mark specified in GB 191.
It must be packed in special steel cylinders. The reusable steel cylinder is coated with aluminum white, and the non-reusable steel cylinder is coated with celestial blue.
The filling coefficient of the bottle must not be greater than 1.02 kg/L.
For reused cylinders, maintain positive
pressure in the cylinder after the product is used.
During loading, unloading and transportation, safety helmets must be worn, and collision, dragging, falling and direct exposure to the sun are prohibited. The transportation of steel cylinders must comply with relevant national or regional regulations.

It must be stored in a cool and dry place, away from heat source, and strictly protected from sun and rain.

Coolant

Common coolant types include isopropanol, ethylene glycol and methanol, which are highly flammable

When the coolant is heated, steam will be generated. To avoid inhalation and burns, wait for the coolant to cool down before operation.

The coolant can be inhaled through the skin and can be hazardous if inhaled in excess. It is very dangerous to ingest coolant by mistake. If ingested, seek medical advice immediately.

Do not contact with any public goods, food or drinking water.

Low-Voltage Battery Acid

For vehicles equipped with ordinary leadacid battery, the gas released during charging is flammable and explosive. Don't use an open flame or spark near a charged or newly charged lead-acid battery. When charging, ensure good ventilation around.

Brake Fluid

Splashing on the skin or eyes will cause slight irritation. Try to avoid contact with the skin and eyes.

It is corrosive to body paint, so be careful not to drop it on the body and painted parts, or wipe off the brake fluid as soon as possible.

### Refrigerant

When operating the braking system, the followings are observed：

For the brake pipeline joint with two fastening nuts, two tools need to be used to operate the nut at the same time when loosening or tightening to prevent the brake pipeline from deformation due to force.
Ensure that the brake hose is naturally bent without distortion or deformation.
Secure the brake pipe with retaining clips to ensure that the pipe does not contact
potential wear areas.
Containers containing brake fluid must be kept clean.
The brake fluid must be sealed during
storage, otherwise it will absorb moisture in the air, reduce the ignition point, and add

failure, which may easily cause danger during use.

Prevent mineral oil from contaminating the brake fluid, or place unused brake fluid into containers that have been filled with mineral oil.

Do not reuse the brake fluid discharged from the vehicle braking system.

Always use clean brake fluid or qualified alternatives to clean hydraulic parts.

After disconnecting the brake pipeline, it is necessary to install suitable end caps or plugs immediately to prevent foreign matters from entering.

Only use brake pipeline fittings or vents that have suitable threads.

Keep the hydraulic parts absolutely clean when working on them.

Fuel

Gasoline and diesel are included. For fuel vehicles, gasoline is extremely volatile and flammable and avoids to be exposed to air, especially in confined space. Avoid naked flame and high temperature near the fuel.

### Kerosene

It is commonly used as a heating fuel, solvent and detergent.

Flammables, strictly comply with the regulations on no-smoking.

Irritation is caused to the mouth and throat if swallowed. This can be even more dangerous if fluids are sucked into the lungs by swallowing.

Contact with the skin can dry it out and cause allergies or dermatitis. Splash in the eye may cause mild discomfort.

Under normal conditions, its low volatility does not cause harmful vapors. Avoid exposure to high temperatures. Avoid contacting with skin and eyes, and make sure the environment is well ventilated.

Lubricant and Grease

Avoid prolonged or repeated body contact with lubricant or grease. All lubricants and greases may irritate to eyes and skin.

Used lubricating oil

Prolonged and repeated exposure to mineral oil can cause loss of natural skin fat,

resulting in dryness, irritation and dermatitis. In addition, used lubricating oil contain potentially harmful contaminants that can cause cancer. Appropriate skin protection methods and cleaning equipment must be provided.

Environmental precautions

Combustion of used lubricating oil in smaller heaters or boilers is limited to units permitted by the design. In case of doubt, contact the relevant local government authorities and the manufacturer of the licensed product.

It is forbidden to discharge lubricant and grease into the environment.

Acids and Alkalis

A material commonly used for battery and cleaning, such as corrosive sodium carbonate or sulfuric acid. Avoid splashing on skin, eyes and clothing. Wear appropriate protective aprons, gloves, and goggles. Do not inhale the mist.

It is irritating and aggressive to the skin, eyes, nose and throat, causing burns and destroying the ordinary protective clothing.

For usage, make sure to provide eye wash, shower and soap, etc. for emergency treatment in case of contact.

There must be danger signs at the storage place.

Solvent

Commonly used solvents include acetone, petroleum solvent oil, toluene, xylene, and trichloroethane. Used for cleaning and dewaxing materials, paints, plastics, resins and thinners.

Some solvents are highly flammable.

Repeated or prolonged skin contact can degrease the skin and cause skin irritation and dermatitis. Some may be inhaled through the skin and increased damage to humans.

Splashing into the eyes may cause severe irritation and blindness.

Brief exposure to high concentrations of vapors or fumes may cause eye and throat irritation, drowsiness, dizziness, headache and loss of consciousness in severe cases.

Repeated or prolonged exposure to excessive but low concentrations of vapors or fumes

may result in more serious personal injury consequences.

Choking the solvent into the lungs due to vomiting can result in serious consequences.

Avoid splashing on skin, eyes and clothing. Protective gloves, goggles and protective clothing must be worn when working.

Ensure good ventilation during use, avoid inhalation of fumes, steam and spray, and keep the container tightly sealed. Do not use in a closed environment.

### Kerosene

When spraying organic solvents such as paints, adhesion agents, coatings, etc., special ventilation equipment or personal respiratory protection device must be used in case of poor ventilation conditions.

Do not heat or ignite the solvent unless specifically instructed by the manufacturer.

Adhesion Agent and Sealing Material

As for the highly flammable, please strictly follow the regulations of no smoking.

Pay attention to the cleanliness and tidiness of items during use, such as covering the seat with disposable paper; The applicators, secondary containers and other containers must be used as much as possible with appropriate labels.

Solvent-based adhesion agent/sealing material

Follow the manufacturer's instructions. See "Solvents" in this section for solvent notes.

Water-based adhesion agent sealing materials

Polymeric emulsions and rubber latex-based materials may contain small amounts of volatile toxic and hazardous chemicals. Avoid contact with skin and eyes, pay attention to ventilation as well.

Hot melt adhesion agent

In the solid state, they are harmless. In the melted state, it may cause burns or health hazards due to inhalation of toxic fumes. Wear proper protective clothing and pay attention to ventilation when using. The heater must have a temperature control function with automatic cut-off.

Resin-type adhesion agent sealing material Examples include epoxides and resin-based formaldehydes. As hazardous or toxic volatile chemicals may be released, they must be mixed in a well-ventilated area.

If the skin comes into direct contact with untreated resins and hardeners, it will absorb toxic and harmful chemicals and cause allergies and dermatitis. Splashes may injure eyes.

Anaerobic cyanoacrylate adhesion agent (super glue) and other acrylic adhesion agent

Most of them are irritants that can cause skin and respiratory allergies or injuries, and some are irritant to eyes.

Follow the manufacturer's instructions to avoid contact with skin and eyes.

Cyanoacrylate adhesion agent (super glue)

Do not contact skin or eyes. If the skin or eye tissue is bonded, cover it with a clean wet towel and seek medical advice immediately. Do not attempt to tear off the bond. Because the vapor can irritate the nose and eyes, it must be used in a well-ventilated area.

For dual combination systems, refer to "Resin Adhesion Agent/Sealant Material" and "Isocyanate Adhesion Agent/Sealant Material" in this section.

Isocyanate ( Polyurethane) adhesion agent / Sealant

Persons with asthma or respiratory sensitivity must not handle or approach these materials to avoid allergic reactions.

Prolonged exposure can irritate eyes and respiratory system. Excessive concentration will affect the nervous system, such as drowsiness. In extreme conditions, shock may occur due to loss of consciousness. Prolonged exposure to high concentrations of vapors can cause adverse health effects. Prolonged skin contact can lead to degrease, skin irritation and dermatitis in some cases. Splashes into the eyes can cause eye discomfort and damage.

### Kerosene

Carry out spraying at the exhaust vent, keep the steam and mist droplets away from the breathing area, and wear appropriate gloves, goggles and respiratory protection devices.

Foam Material

Generally used for noise isolation materials. Treated foam materials is used in seats and upholstery to enhance carpet comfort and to protect feet in the event of a crash.

Persons with chronic respiratory conditions, asthma, bronchial conditions, or a history of allergies cannot work in or near untreated materials. Its parts, vapors or sprays can cause direct irritation, sensitive reactions and may even be toxic or harmful.

Avoid breathing vapors and sprays. These materials must be used under the premise of good ventilation and respiratory protection. Remove the respirator after the vapor/spray has completely dissipated, otherwise the vapor and mist will be inhaled into the body.

The combustion of foam materials will produce toxic and harmful fumes. It is not allowed to smoke, use open flame or electrical equipment in the foaming operation until the vapor disappears completely. The thermal cutting of any foam materials or specially-treated foam materials must be carried out with guaranteed ventilation.

Chemical Material

Chemical materials such as solvents, sealing materials, adhesion agents, paints, resin foam materials, low voltage battery acids, high voltage battery electrolytes, coolants, brake fluids, lubricating oils, and greases must be stored and handled with care. They may be toxic, harmful, corrosive, irritating or highly flammable, producing harmful fumes and dust.

Operating instructions for chemical materials:

Please carefully read and follow the hazard warnings and protective requirements on the labels, accompanying instructions or other instructions on the material container. Material health and safety data sheets may be obtained from the manufacturer. Chemical materials must be removed from skin and clothing immediately after contamination. Wash or discard heavily contaminated clothing. Organize work practices, wear protective clothing to avoid contamination of skin and eyes, inhalation of vapors, mist, dust or fumes, improper labeling of containers, and avoid fire and explosion hazards.

After handling chemical materials, wash your hands before work breaks, eating, smoking, drinking or using the toilet.
Keep the workplace clean, tidy and free of spills.
Store chemical materials in accordance with relevant national and local regulations.
Keep chemical materials out of the reach of children.

Operational prohibitions for chemical materials.

Do not mix chemical materials without the manufacturer's instructions. Some chemical materials can form other toxic and harmful chemical materials when mixed, and release the toxic fumes or become explosive

Do not spray chemical materials, especially solvent-based materials, in a closed environment, for example, when someone is inside the vehicle.

Do not bring chemical materials close to heat sources or open flames without the guidance of the manufacturer. Some are highly flammable, and some may release toxic or harmful smoke.

### Kerosene

Never leave the container open. The flue gas emitted can accumulate to toxic, hazardous or explosive concentrations. Some of the flue gases are heavier than air and will collect in confined space, such as in a well.

Do not transfer chemical materials into unmarked containers.

Anticorrosive Material

It is highly flammable and explosive, and strictly abides by the prohibition of fireworks.

There are many kinds of these materials, including solvents, resins or petroleum products, and the manufacturer's instructions must be followed. Avoid contact with skin and eyes. They can only be sprayed in wellventilated and unconfined spaces.

Fiber Insulation Material

Generally used as sound insulation material.

The fiber surface and cut edge can irritate the skin, which is usually a physical effect rather than a chemical reaction.

Precautions such as the use of gloves must be taken to avoid excessive skin contact.

### Fluororubber

Usually used to make O-ring, seals or cylinder pads and other parts.

Fluororubber is a kind of fluoroelastomer, as fluorine-contained synthetic rubber.

The fluororubber is very safe to use under normal conditions. However, if exposed to temperatures above 400 C, the material will not burn but will decompose, and one of the substances produced is hydrofluoric acid. The hydrofluoric acid is highly corrosive and can be absorbed directly into the body by contacting.

O-ring, seal, or gasket, etc., which are exposed to high temperatures, will char or turn to a black and sticky substance. Do not touch them or the objects to which they are attached under any circumstances.

Consultation must be made first to determine whether fluororubber or other fluoroelastomer are contained in the affected O-ring, seal or gasket. If there is uncertainty, be careful, because the material of such parts is likely to be fluororubber or other fluoroelastomer.

If fluororubber or other fluoroelastomer have been exposed to high temperatures, areas likely to be affected must be carefully cleaned before work commences. Disposable hazardous protective plastic gloves must always be worn, the acids must be neutralized with steel balls and limewater (with sodium hydroxide) before disposing of decomposed fluororubber residues and final cleaning of the area, the affected area must be cleaned with clean water, and discarded plastic gloves must be disposed with care.

Soldering Tin

Soldering tin is a mixture of metals that have a lower melting point than structural metals (usually lead and tin). If a gas-air flame is used to heat the soldering tin, the use of soldering tin usually does not produce toxic plumes. Do not use acetylene-oxygen flame to heat the soldering tin, because the temperature is too high and lead gas is easily generated, which will cause poisoning if inhaled by the human body.

The use of any flame on a greasecoated soldering tin may produce certain gases. Inhalation of these gases must be avoided.

Care must be taken when removing excess soldering tin to avoid inhaling fine lead dust. Use respiratory protective equipment if necessary.

Spilled soldering tin and filings must be collected and removed immediately to avoid electrical short circuit and environmental pollution.

After working with the welding tongs, clean the hands or clothing in case of touching the soldering tin to avoid body ingestion.

Dust and Powder

Powders, dusts or motes may be irritating, harmful or toxic. Avoid inhaling in powdery chemical materials or dust caused by dry friction operation. If ventilation is poor, wear respirator protection.

The fine dusts of combustible substances may have the risk of explosion. Keep away from open flames or sparks.

Electric Shock

Electric shock can result from leakage of high voltage component, the use of faulty components, or improper operation of normal equipment.

The orange cable on the vehicle is a high voltage cable, and the part with the high voltage logo is a high voltage component.

### Fluororubber

Such components are particularly dangerous when the vehicle is in a strong electric state or when such components are damaged. Do not touch them at will.

Electrical safety precautions:

Ensure that the electrical equipment is well maintained and inspected frequently. Faulty equipment must be marked and preferably removed.
Ensure that wires, cables, and connectors are not worn, kinked, cut, broken, or
damaged.
Make sure that the electrical equipment and cables do not come into contact with other liquids such as coolant and water.
Ensure that the electrical equipment is
protected by the correct rated fuse.

Do not use the electrical equipment incorrectly, and in any wrong way. The consequences may be fatal. Ensure that the cables of the movable electrical equipment are not tangled or damaged, such as when lifting the vehicle. Ensure that the staff concerned have received basic first aid training.

In case of electric shock:

Turn off the power before contacting the injured person.
If the power cannot be turned off, push or drag the victim away from the power source with dry insulating material.
If the injured person becomes unconscious after being away from the danger of power supply, perform proper CPR immediately. Seek medical advice immediately.

For hybrid and pure electric vehicles, the operation of high voltage system must comply with the following items:

The maintenance of high voltage system components must be carried out by
qualified maintenance technicians. Improper maintenance may cause injury to personnel, vehicles or equipment.
The voltage of high voltage systems can
reach several hundred volts or more. During the removal and installation of high voltage components, PPE such as insulating gloves and high voltage insulating shoes must
always be worn.
Before repairing, disassembling and
assembling the high voltage components, the vehicle must be powered off at high
voltage, and it must be confirmed that the negative cable of iron battery has been
disconnected, and the vehicle must be kept still for more than 5 minutes.
If the maintenance area is close to the
high voltage component, the ignition/start/ stop button must be switched off and the vehicle must be kept still for more than 5
minutes before repairing.
Do not put the power battery pack near open flame or heat.
The power battery pack contains acidic
electrolyte. Avoid contact with eyes, skin and clothing. In case of accident, flush with clean

water and seek medical advice immediately.

In case of severe collision or flooding, the power battery pack of the vehicle may be damaged or the vehicle cannot be driven away from the flooded area, the power supply must be cut off if it is safe to do so. When conditions permit, conduct the vehicle high voltage power-off and disconnect the low voltage battery (lead-acid battery or start iron battery) negative cables, and take rescue measures in accordance with regulations. Keep a safe distance from the vehicle and place high voltage warning signs around the vehicle.

### Fluororubber

Charging

Electromagnetic radiation will be generated when the vehicle is being charged. Persons with implanted pacemakers or defibrillators must not approach the vehicle (including entering the vehicle and loading and unloading items in the trunk).

Before charging, ensure that the socket of the charger is dry. During charging, ensure that the charging connection part is not wetted by rain or other liquids.

Fire

Many materials related to vehicle maintenance are highly flammable. Some materials may produce toxic or harmful gases after they are burned.

When storing and handling flammable and explosive materials or solvents, it is necessary to follow safety regulations, especially when approaching electrical equipment or during welding operations.

Where welding or heating equipment is used, appropriate fire extinguisher must be provided.

In case of fire in the vehicle, if the vehicle catches fire, the following operations must be carried out while ensuring the safety of personnel:

Turn off the ignition switch or start/stop button and find a nearby dry powder fire extinguisher to put out the open fire.
Call the local rescue telephone for rescue immediately.
Carry out vehicle high voltage power-off
and disconnect the negative cable of lowvoltage battery (lead-acid battery or start iron battery) when possible.

If the fire is large, stay away from the vehicle. Fire Extinguisher

The vehicle is equipped with a dry powder fire extinguisher, which is suitable for extinguishing the initial fire of oil, flammable gas, electrical equipment, etc.

For some highly diffusible gases such as hydrogen and acetylene, it is difficult to dilute the gas after injection of dry powder fire extinguisher, and for precision instruments, it will leave dry powder residue. These situations are not applicable for dry powder fire extinguisher.

You must follow the instructions on the fire extinguisher. Do not use the fire extinguisher in the unapplicable situations.

Noise

Some operations will generate high noise, so appropriate hearing protection equipment must be worn, otherwise hearing damage may occur.

General Workshop Tools and Equipment

It is important that all tools and equipment are well maintained and the correct safety equipment is provided as specified.

Do not use tools or equipment for purposes other than those for which they are designed. Do not overload equipment such as cranes, jacks, axles and chassis or jacking ropes. Damage caused by overloading is not apparent immediately and may cause fatal injuries when the device is used later.

Never use damaged or faulty tools or equipment, especially high-speed equipment such as grinding mill. Damaged grinding mill may break down at any time and cause serious injury.

Wear safety goggles when using a grinding mill, chisel, or sandblasting device.

When using sandblasting equipment, handling asbestosbased materials or using spray equipment, a suitable breathing mask must be worn.

Ensure adequate ventilation to control dust, fumes and gases.

### Fluororubber

Suspended Load

Never use non-special equipment to lift the vehicle to avoid injury due to sliding.

There is always a danger when heavy objects are lifted or suspended. Never work under heavy objects that are not supported, suspended, or lifted, such as lifted powertrain.

Ensure that lifting equipment such as lift, jack, hoists, axle seats and slings are suitable for the type of work and kept are in good condition and properly maintained.

Warning Markings on Vehicles, Equipment or Premises

Warning label may be indicated on some vehicle parts, equipment and places for display.

Do not move these warning labels and make sure that their contents are clear and visible. The purpose of these warning labels is to remind the relevant personnel to pay attention. If the relevant personnel cannot see the labels, they may ignore these warnings, causing potential hazards.

### Electrical Safety

Dangerous current

Alternating current above 25V and direct current above 60V are dangerous.
The maximum permissible touch voltage in Germany (according to the VDE standard) is 50 VAC and 120 VDC.
The current of about 5mA passing through the human body can be regarded as
an "electrical accident", which will cause
numbness, but the current can still be
conducted.

The current of about 10mA passing through the human body reaches the limit of derived current, and in this case, the human body begins to contract and can no longer conduct current. The retention time of the current also increases accordingly.

Prolonged retention of 30 to 50mA AC may cause respiratory arrest and ventricular fibrillation.

The current of about 80mA passing through the human body is considered a "deadly current".

AC voltage creates alternating current in the human body, which causes fibrillation of muscle tissue and the heart.

Lower frequency of AC voltage will pose a higher danger!

Alternating current can trigger ventricular fibrillation, which will be fatal if no first aid is given!

Human body internal resistance

For high currents caused by high voltages, the corresponding resistance values in the human body are very low, especially the blood in all blood vessels is a very good conductor. The contact points in electrical accidents are different, and the impact on the human body is correspondingly different.

Skin resistance values vary widely. (depending on skin hardness, humidity, conductivity) However, the skin resistance corresponding to the voltages over 100V is almost 0 Ω. The skin is completely penetrated.

If the alternating current stays in the heart for about 10--15 milliseconds, it will be fatal! (ventricular fibrillation).

Electrical Accident

Consequences of electric shock and accident Electric shock effect:

The current lower than the conduction limit will cause a corresponding electric shock, which may easily lead to injury due to uncontrolled and unbalanced limbs!

Thermal effect:

Burns and coking may occur at the current lead-in and lead-out points, and internal burns may also be possible. These may cause the kidney overloaded and even fatal injury!

Chemical effect:

Blood and cellular fluids become electrolytes and are electrolyzed. These may cause severe poisoning, which will not be discovered until several days later, so the damage is enormous!

Muscle stimulation effect:

All body functions and human muscle movements are controlled by the brain through electrical stimulation of the nervous system. If the current through the human body is too high, the muscles start twitching and the brain can no longer control the muscle tissue.

Thermal effect of static short circuit:

Excessive heating of the tool may cause the material to be melt and even a burning accident!

Spark due to short circuit:

The metal will melt quickly, producing flying sparks, and the temperature of the flying metal particles exceeds 5000℃. These may cause burns and serious eye damage!

### Electrical Safety

Arc light generated when live high voltage lines are connected and disconnected:

Optical radiation may cause electric ophthalmia!

First aid measures for electric shock accidents

The following first-aid measures must be taken to rescue the injured in the electrical accident:

1. Human safety comes first, never touch people who are still in contact with voltage.
2. If possible, immediately de-energize the electrical system (turn the ignition switch off or remove the maintenance switch immediately)!
3. Isolate the accident victim or electrical conductors from the voltage with a nonconductive object (board, broom handle, etc.).

### Safe Maintenance

Personnel Requirements

Personnel allocation

1. Maintenance technicians:

Maintenance operators with qualifications for the maintenance of pure electric and hybrid models are responsible for vehicle inspection and maintenance as described below:

a. Routine maintenance
b. Inspection and maintenance of non-high voltage components;
c. Inspection and maintenance of non-high voltage circuits;

### 2. Supervisors:

Maintenance technicians with qualifications for the maintenance of pure electric and hybrid models are responsible for supervising the whole process of maintenance as described below:

a. Supervise whether the composition of maintenance personnel, use of tools, wearing of PPE, safety protection of spare parts, and the maintenance safety warning signs meet the requirements; b. Check the emergency maintenance switch on and off (if equipped) check the vehicle power on and off; c. Check the safety maintenance operation procedures in the maintenance process, and guide the operators according to the safety maintenance operation procedures; the maintenance personnel must inform the supervisor after completing an operation, and the supervisor must make marks in the operation flow sheet; d. The supervisors must take responsibility seriously to ensure the safety of the maintenance process and avoid safety liability accidents. 3. In addition to the maintenance technician, a supervisor must be provided for the inspection and maintenance of the high voltage circuits.

Personnel qualification

Maintenance technicians for new energy vehicles must have the following qualifications:

1. Special Appliance Operation Certificate (Electrician) recognized by the state.
2. Junior (and above) Electrician's Certificate for (vocational qualification)
3. The corresponding maintenance qualification certificate for pure electric and hybrid models granted by BYD Auto Sales Co., Ltd.
4. And other requirements of local regulations, if any.

Equipment Inspection

1. Insulation equipment and safety protection equipment must be inspected for damage, metal puncture, etc. before each use, and if any, they must not be used; 2. Insulation equipment and safety protection equipment must be tested for moisture, water and dirt before each use, and if any, they must be restored to performance before use; 3. Set the megohmmeter to 1000VDC to detect the insulation resistance of the weakest part of the insulation equipment every month. If the resistance is less than 2MΩ, the insulation equipment must not be used.

Inspection of High Voltage Circuits

Non-live inspection

1. Power off the vehicle.

a. Set the vehicle to OFF and keep it stationary for 5min.
b. Power off the low voltage electrical system. See
c. Disconnect the power maintenance switch (if equipped);
d. Disconnect the positive and negative busbars of the power battery;
e. Insulate and seal the positive and negative busbar connectors of the power battery and the harness connectors to prevent short circuits and foreign objects. Note: Operators in steps 3, 4, and 5, and e must wear insulating shoes, insulating gloves and insulating pads.

2. Inspection of high voltage circuits other than power battery.

a. 3 min after the completion of the poweroff link of the vehicle, use a multimeter to measure the voltage between the positive and negative terminals (one-handed operation) before testing the peripheral high voltage parts, which must be less than 60V DC.

b. When the measurement voltage is less than 60V DC, the high voltage circuits and components other than the power battery can be detected normally. When the measured voltage is greater than 60V DC, do not perform any operation until the voltage drops to within 60V DC.

c. During removal of the high voltage connector, it is necessary to insulate and seal the high voltage connector with insulating tape to prevent short circuit and foreign objects.

3. Inspection of high voltage battery. Refer to live maintenance below.

Live inspection

1. Charging fault inspection.

a. Wear protective equipment according to personnel and protective equipment.
b. Connect the body to the protective ground wire;
c. Refer to the service manual to measure the corresponding parameters depending on the faults. During the measurement process, the following principles must be observed:

When using a multimeter to measure high voltage, it is necessary to select the correct range. The accuracy of the multimeter used for testing must not be lower than 0.5. It is required to set the multimeter to AC/DC voltage, the AC range must be greater than 400V AC for AC input detection of charging equipment, and the selected test range for DC output side must be greater than that when the multimeter is set to DC of the total voltage of the power battery of the vehicle under test.

Ⅱ. The multimeter and other testing equipment used are equipped with insulated alligator clips on one probe (required with a withstand voltage of 3kV and an overcurrent capability greater than 5A). When measuring, first clip the alligator clip to one terminal of the circuit, and then connect another probe to the terminal to be measured to measure the reading. Hold the probe with only one hand at each measurement. During the measurement process, it is strictly forbidden to operate and touch the metal part of the probe with both hands.

d. During replacement of high voltage components and harness connectors, the disconnected connectors must be insulated and sealed to prevent short circuit and foreign objects; e. It is strictly forbidden to disconnect the high/low-voltage connectors when the load is live, otherwise it may cause personal injury and damage to the vehicle. f. It is strictly forbidden to disconnect the low-voltage connectors when the power is ON, otherwise the vehicle may be damaged. g. For models that require tooling for high voltage detection, live measurement is strictly prohibited when there is no tooling.

2. Inspection of high voltage circuits and components.

a. Wear protective equipment according to personnel and protective equipment. b. Refer to the service manual to measure the corresponding parameters depending on the faults. During the measurement process, the following principles must be observed:

When using a multimeter to measure high voltage, it is necessary to select the correct range. The accuracy of the multimeter used for testing must not be lower than 0.5. It is required to set the multimeter to DC voltage, and the selected range must be greater than that when the multimeter is set to DC of the total voltage of the power battery of the vehicle under test.

Ⅱ. The multimeter and other testing equipment used are equipped with insulated alligator clips on one probe (required with a withstand voltage of 3kV and an overcurrent capability greater than 5A). When measuring, first clip the alligator clip to one terminal of the circuit, and then connect another probe to the terminal to be measured to measure the reading. Hold the probe with only one hand at each measurement. During the measurement process, it is strictly forbidden to operate and touch the metal part of the probe with both hands.

### Battery Safety

Risk Identification

Risky vehicle

The power battery is risky if the vehicle is in the following states:

1. The wading depth of the vehicle reaches door sills and there is no water inside, with wading time more than 30 min.
2. The high and low voltage connectors of the power battery are soaked in water.
3. The power battery suffers deformation, puncture and electrolyte leakage after a collision.

4. A fire breaks out in the vehicle.

Risk judgment

When a risky vehicle is to be transferred or enters the service store, a portable infrared thermal imager or infrared thermometer must be used to detect the highest temperature point of the power battery at the first time;

Portable infrared thermal imager/infrared thermometer: the measuring range must be -50 C\~380 C.

1. If the temperature of the damaged part of the battery pack is higher than the ambient temperature by 10° C or there is an obvious temperature rise (2° C/minute) in the ambient temperature.

Note: In this case, it is required to spray a large amount of water to cool the battery pack until the temperature drops below the ambient temperature;

2. The battery tray is seriously deformed (with depression depth of the bearing area more than 10mm) and damaged.

3. The battery has been ablated by flame or baked for a long time (flame distance > 10cm, duration > 10 min).

4. The battery has been ablated by flame, resulting in ablation marks, and baked at close distance (flame distance < 10cm, duration ＞ 3 min).

5. Electrical leakage is reported after wading and wading time exceeds 30 min.

6. The battery tray is damaged or leaks electrolyte.

The vehicle is highly risky if any of the above conditions is met.

Risk Handling

Transportation of risky vehicle

For vehicles that need to be transferred to the service store for maintenance, the risk level must be judged according to the risk identification contents, and corresponding pretransportation treatment must be carried out according to the risk level:

1. For risky vehicles, a portable infrared thermal imager or infrared thermometer must be used to detect the highest temperature point of the power battery. Vehicles with no abnormal temperature and no high risk can be normally transferred to the service store for further maintenance.

2. For vehicles with abnormal temperature or high risk, the battery pack must be cooled by spraying a large amount of water. After the fire is extinguished, the battery pack must be continuously cooled with water for more than 30 min until the temperature drops below the ambient temperature before transportation.

For batteries with abnormal temperature, it is required to re-measure the temperature every 5min during transportation to judge whether cooling is needed. For high-risk vehicles with no abnormal temperature, it is required to re-measure the temperature every 10 min during transportation to judge whether cooling is needed.

Note: It is recommended that when possible, a temperature monitoring system must be used to monitor the temperature of the battery pack throughout the transportation, with not less than 8 temperature monitoring points.

### Battery Safety

Handling of risky vehicle

After a risky vehicle arrives at the service store, the risk level must be judged according to the risk identification contents, and corresponding treatment must be carried out according to the risk level:

1. For risky vehicles, a portable infrared thermal imager or infrared thermometer must be used to detect the highest temperature point of

the power battery. Vehicles with no abnormal temperature and no high risk must be overhauled normally according to the Service Manual, and the battery temperature must be measured every 1 hour during maintenance. It can be judged that the battery is risk-free if there is no abnormality over 12 hours.

2. For vehicles with abnormal temperature or high risk, the battery pack must be cooled by spraying a large amount of water until the temperature drops below the ambient temperature before the next operation can be carried out. The specific operation is as follows:

a. When a vehicle with abnormal temperature enters the service store, it must be cooled immediately (at the same time, the lowvoltage power supply of the vehicle must be switched off) until the temperature drops below the ambient temperature before the next operation is carried out;

b. After the vehicle with abnormal temperature cools down or for the highrisk vehicle, it is required to remove the battery pack at the first time. The removal process must follow Chapter III Safe Maintenance. At the same time, the temperature of the power battery must be monitored throughout the process. For abnormal temperature rise, a large amount of water is needed for cooling;

c. The power battery must be transferred to a safe area immediately after removal and the seal cover must be removed (for a glued seal cover, cut it off directly with a knife, and pay attention to avoiding scratches). and the connecting pieces and BIC connectors between all modules must be quickly disconnected with electric insulating tools;

d. All deformed and overheating modules must be taken out separately and soaked in 3.6% brine. During the soaking process, a large amount of hydrogen and oxygen will be produced by electrolysis. The soaking location must be far away from fire sources and well ventilated. Operators must not wear any metal ornaments to avoid sparks during operation. Pay

attention to avoiding static electricity in dry environment, which can be eliminated by spraying water. After immersion in 3.6% brine for 12 hours, the measured voltage of the module must be lower than 1/2 of the nominal voltage, and then the module can be dried with an air gun and then moved to the high-risk battery storage area.

All other modules must be hoisted out of the tray synchronously, dried with an air gun, loaded back to the tray and transferred to the high-risk battery storage area, and each module must be discharged to 5% SOC by using discharging equipment.

Note: When there is no water inside the power battery, only the deformed or overheating modules need to be hoisted out, and the rest modules can remain in the tray. The connecting pieces and BIC connectors between modules must be disconnected and then these modules can be stored after discharging.

### Battery Safety

e. In case of flooding, breakage and overheating of sampling lines, it is required to open the side covers of each module and cut off the sampling lines of all conductors (cutting off 1cm length close to the conductor to prevent re-contact). This operation is only applicable to batteries with wires as sampling lines in centralized BMS, instead of batteries with FPC sampling lines in distributed BMS;

f. For maintenance after battery disassembly, see Safe Maintenance

Storage and Transportation of High-Risk Batteries

### Storage condition

The high-risk battery storage area must meet the following requirements:

1. The stored high-risk batteries must be discharged and dried. At the same time, the batteries of various risk levels must be classified and separately placed in the storage area, and relevant identification (vehicle information, fault conditions, etc.) must be made. Leaking batteries must be stored after anti-corrosion and anti-leakage packaging;

2. The storage site must be a separate storage area for risky batteries. It must be far away from the production area, and have warning signs such as High Voltage and Danger. Other materials or personnel are prohibited from approaching. The site must have basic monitoring facilities and be inspected regularly.

3. c. Stacking is prohibited. Steel multi-layer shelves can be used (the bearing weight of each layer must be greater than twice the specified weight of stored batteries, and the shelf must be clearly marked with specified bearing capacity). At the same time, the batteries must be placed horizontally, rather than obliquely, upside down or horizontally, and no items must be placed on the batteries to avoid battery damage caused by compression.

4. The storage environment must be kept ventilated and dry, avoid direct sunlight, exposure to sunlight or rain, with favorable dust prevention, waterproof and anti-static protection. The storage temperature of the battery must be controlled within - 20 ℃ 45 ℃ and the humidity must be 5-95%.

5. The storage area must be equipped with fire-fighting facilities such as smoke alarm, automatic sprinkler system and automatic smoke removal system (infrared temperature monitoring system is recommended at the same time to achieve remote alarm of abnormal temperature).

### Transportation conditions

The transportation of high-risk batteries must meet the following requirements:

1. High-risk batteries to be transported must have been discharged and dried, and have no abnormal temperature rise over 24 hours. 2. Protective packaging (with waterproof, moisture-proof, anti-static and anticorrosion measures) must be used for highrisk batteries to be transported; 3. The road must be unblocked. Direct sunlight must be avoided within the scope of loading activities, and flammable, explosive and hazardous chemicals must not exist. Water and other liquids must not enter the battery.

Outdoor loading must be suspended in case of bad weather such as rain.

4. Requirements for transport equipment Professional equipment and tools such as electric forklift and manual forklift with proper carrying capacity must be used for handling and placing traction batteries, so as to avoid damage to traction batteries during handling.

5. Requirements for transport vehicles A closed compartment must be used for transporting high-risk batteries to prevent rainwater from entering the batteries during transportation. Traction batteries must be transported separately. If other items need to be loaded on the transport vehicle together, liquid, flammable, explosive and hazardous chemicals are prohibited;

6. During handling of traction batteries with equipment, the equipment must be operated by professionals and careful handling is required; throwing, rolling and heavy pressure are prohibited. Packaged traction batteries must be loaded from the warehouse, rather than loaded halfway or stacked on the transport vehicle, to prevent the traction batteries from heavy pressure.

Requirements for transportation process Land transportation: during transportation, squeeze and bumps between batteries or between battery and the transport vehicle body due to sudden braking must be avoided; during transportation, the storage temperature of the power battery must be -20° C to 45 C, the humidity be 5-95%, and the transport time controlled within 72 hours. If the time is exceeded, special treatment must be done to control the temperature and humidity to ensure that the product is not wet or exposed to the sun; shipping and air transport: Special packaging certified must be used for shipping and air transport, and shipping and air transport are not allowed in case of ordinary packaging; air transport must meet MH/T1020-2009 and pass UN38.3 test. The ambient temperature around the power battery packing box must not exceed 45° C, and it must be ensured that the product is not wet or exposed to the sun.

8. Emergency handling in land transportation.

a. In case of electrolyte leakage of traction batteries, stop transportation and contact relevant BYD after-sales personnel for handling. If the electrolyte of the power battery splashes on the skin and eyes, please rinse the skin and eyes with plenty of water immediately for more than 15 min, and then seek medical treatment.

b. When the power battery catches fire, please use a non-water-based fire extinguisher to extinguish the fire. If the fire is large, it can be extinguished with a large amount of water. Afterwards, the power battery needs to be cooled with water for 30 min.

### Transportation conditions

c. During transportation, if the battery packing box is accidentally wet by water, the packing box must be removed immediately to avoid the wet packing box becoming a conductor causing battery discharge or burning battery terminals;

d. In case of bumps and severe squeeze during transportation of the traction batteries, the transportation must be stopped, and can continue until professionals eliminate potential safety hazards.

9. Requirements for unloading The unloading environment and equipment are the same as the loading and the unloading and storage place must avoid direct sunlight, and be not less than 2m from heat sources; before unloading, check whether the power battery packing box is damaged on the transport vehicle. Pay attention to the height of the compartment when unloading, and prevent the battery from being damaged due to the collision between the forklift truck and the compartment.

### A Caution:

Please operate the lifting vehicle as follows. Please see the instructions of the lift if special operation is required.

### A Caution:

Please operate the lifting vehicle as follows. Please see the instructions of the lift if special operation is required.

1. Drive the vehicle into the center of the lift to make sure that it is equal to the front and rear support point of the lift.
2. Place the support point of 4 positions of the lift directly below the vehicle lifting support point and adjust the lift support point to be the same as the vehicle lifting support point.
3. Operate the lift slowly so that the support point of the lift is just in contact with the vehicle lifting support point and slightly stressed.
4. Make a recheck that the support point of the lift 4 positions are aligned with the vehicle lifting support point. If there is any deviation, it is necessary to lower the lift slightly, and repeat the above steps 2 and 3 until all support points are aligned.
5. Operate the lift to raise to a proper height. During the lifting of the vehicle, always
1. Drive the vehicle into the center of the lift platform to ensure that the distances in all directions are equal.
2. Perform the parking brake to ensure that the vehicle is firmly seated on the lifting platform.
3. Operate the lift slowly to raise the vehicle to a suitable height. During the lifting of the vehicle, always pay attention to whether there are objects around and below the vehicle or personnel approaching.
4. Lock the lift to ensure that the lift safety mechanism has been correctly applied.
5. When lowering the vehicle, make sure again that there is no person or equipment directly under the vehicle.
6. Release the lift safety mechanism, and slowly lower the vehicle by operating the lift. Always pay attention to whether there is any interference of objects or persons around and under the vehicle during lowering.
7. After the lift is lowered to the lowest position, the vehicle must be driven out.

The original tow hook must be used to tow the vehicle, otherwise tow hook of other brands or sizes cannot be securely installed to the vehicle.

### ? Warning:

Situation in which low voltage electrical system power off must be performed: Before repairing any electrical component, low voltage electrical system power off must be performed following the requirements below, and low voltage electrical system power on must be performed after the repairment, unless otherwise specified in the operation procedure. – Low voltage electrical system power off is also required if the tool or device is easily accessible to the start iron battery poles and cable connectors. Violation of these safety warnings may result in personal injury or vehicle damage.

Power-off of low-voltage electrical system

1. Turn off all electrical appliances, and the power supply of the vehicle (by pressing the "START/STOP" button).

![](images/7b07361808cf88dc614a35165c55d11cbe8fa27f3330a5f27cdbfded039b3f95.webp)

2. Detach 4 fixing clips with a plastic pry plate and take out the carpet access cover.

![](images/6b61ab4708003d3a20e78fe7766a9d2daedd2a7a2086c6ed697b640ae810c106.webp)

3. Unscrew 1 tightening nut and disconnect the negative cable of the 12 V battery.

Tightening torque: 9 ±1 N•m

### A Caution:

After the negative cable joint is disconnected, the negative terminal of the 12 V battery must be insulated and packaged to prevent it from contacting other metals in the vehicle and causing circuit safety hazards.

Power-on of low-voltage electrical system

1. Before power-on, make sure that the electrical circuits of the vehicle are well connected and there is no flammable or explosive article near the negative terminal of the 12 V battery.

2. Install other components in the reverse order of removal.

3. After terminals of the 12 V battery are disconnected, the vehicle may be in a sleep mode. After negative cable joint is installed, the vehicle needs to be awakened by pressing the microswitch on the driver's door handle twice continuously.

### 0 Reminder:

After long-term storage, the start iron battery may also enter the hibernation state. The same method must be used to wake up the sleeper before connecting the vehicle power supply.

4. After wake-up, power on the vehicle (by pressing the "START/STOP" button to switch the power supply to OK mode), and check that the electric appliances of the vehicle are functioning normally. In this case, the lowvoltage electrical system of the vehicle has been powered on.

### A Caution:

If the start iron battery has power loss, the low voltage electrical system of the vehicle may not be powered on normally. At this time, eliminate the power loss fault of the start iron battery first, and then power on again.

### ? Warning:

When high voltage electrical system power-off is required: The high voltage electrical system must be powered off as per the following requirements before maintenance of any high voltage electrical system component and powered on after maintenance unless otherwise specified in the operating procedure.

– All high voltage system harnesses are orange in color. Before carrying out maintenance work on all components of the high voltage system, protective measures must be taken in accordance with the maintenance requirements of the high voltage system, such as wearing insulating gloves, insulating shoes, goggles, laying insulated mats, high voltage hazard warning signs, etc.

The maintenance of the high voltage electrical system must be carried out by the maintenance personnel with the qualification recognized by the company and local laws and regulations. Violation of these safety warnings may result in personal injury or vehicle damage.

4. Wait for 1 min, and use a multimeter with a measuring range ≥ 1000 V (DC) to measure the terminal voltage of connector of high-voltage distribution wiring harness subassembly and that of drive motor control unit assembly.

Voltage standard: ≤60 V (DC) If the voltages of connector terminals are all within the standard range, the highvoltage electrical system of the vehicle has been successfully powered off. It is not allowed to repair the highvoltage system components except the high-voltage distribution wiring harness subassembly and high-voltage battery until the fault is eliminated. ### Description of Vehicle Identification Number

![](images/7389606ac0908423802df3127c2403ea08f3f6ef73e729ecd9c8082230f85783.webp)

Vehicle Identification Number (VIN) is a set of numbers for vehicle identification, consisting of three parts:

1. This is the World Manufacturer Identifier (WMI), which records the geographical area and country of the manufacturer. 2. This is the Vehicle Descriptor Section (VDS), which consists of feature codes such as vehicle type, body type, motor type/ vehicle length, drive type and wheelbase/ axle number, vehicle technical characteristics parameters, and inspection bits. 3. This is the Vehicle Instructor Section (VIS), which consists of 8-digit codes such as year code, assembly plant code and production serial number.

### Description of Vehicle Nameplate

![](images/c78a297bef01bb998af62888cd0e4fae9727460f5519d93c3e55acc40d2a2c2e.webp)

The vehicle nameplate is located under the right B pillar, and the information includes: company name, brand, country of manufacture, vehicle model, number of passengers, manufacture date, model of drive motor, peak power of drive motor, rated voltage of power battery system, rated capacity of power battery system, vehicle identification code, maximum allowable total mass.

Model and coding description of drive motor

![](images/f190e61713774c0adeb960ac62dfb6bcb2e8387988f2ed04767568b52bf22a72.webp)

The model and number of the drive motor are indicated on its nameplate at the bottom of the drive motor.

### Reminder:

In order to keep the power battery in the best condition, the vehicle needs to be fully charged regularly (at least 6 months or 72,000km) to achieve the purpose of battery self-calibration.

Severe operating condition refers to one of the following conditions:

Frequent exposure to dust and salty air.

Frequent driving on bumpy, uneven, wet or mountainous roads.
Driving in cold areas.
Frequent use of brakes and frequent sudden braking.
Frequent towing vehicles.
Used as a taxi.
At a temperature above 32 0 C, more than 50% of the total driving time in congested urban areas.
At a temperature above 30 C, more than 50% of the total driving time at a speed of higher than 120 km/h.

Frequent overload driving.

### A Caution:

Operators shall wear workwear, insulating gloves, insulated shoes, goggles and other insulating protective equipment.

Ensure that the work site is dry and ventilated, tools and instruments are placed neatly, and fire extinguishers are provided when necessary.

Check the use safety of instruments and equipment, such as lifts and jacks.

Check the safe driving and operation conditions of the vehicle to ensure smooth maintenance.

Please put on the seat cover and steering wheel cover when the vehicle enters the site. Avoid contaminating the vehicle during operation.

Before driving into the lift frame, make sure that there is sufficient distance between the bottom and both sides of the vehicle and the lift frame to avoid scratching.

Before lifting the vehicle, make sure that the vehicle weight does not exceed the rated load of the lift.

When lifting the vehicle, be sure to select the correct lifting point.

When lifting the vehicle, it is not allowed to start the vehicle and engage a gear with driving wheels on the ground; otherwise, vehicle damage or personal injury may be caused.

Operators shall strictly abide by various safety rules and use rules during maintenance; otherwise, vehicle damage or personal injury may be caused.

Use original spare parts when replacing components and wearing parts to ensure the safety and performance of the vehicle.

After maintenance, a test drive must be carried out for inspection, with special attention to the brake system and passenger protection system.

The DTCs must be cleared before the vehicle can be handed over to the customer.

### Safe operation guide for maintenance Basic safety requirements

1. The signs marked on the vehicle, such as "WARNING" and "CAUTION", are safety prompt information. For maintenance or repair, relevant prompts and specified safe operation requirements shall be strictly followed.

"WARNING": Serious injury or death will be caused if the specified operating procedures are not followed. "CAUTION": Immediate danger, which may cause serious personal injury if the specified operating procedures are not followed.

2. High-voltage components include: high voltage orange wiring harness, high-voltage battery system, front drive electric powertrain, rear drive electric powertrain, charging and distribution assembly, charging system, electric compressor and PTC heater.

3. Electrical circuit maintenance personnel must hold high-voltage electrical practice qualification certificates and strictly abide by electrician safety operation procedures.

4. During maintenance of high-voltage components, maintenance personnel must wear non-destructive insulation protective equipment as required, and the maintenance tools used must be high-voltage insulation tools.

5. During vehicle maintenance, do not wear ornaments or watches.

6. Non-professionals are strictly prohibited from cutting or opening high-voltage cables and components.

7. Do not simultaneously touch both the positive and negative terminals of a high-voltage component with both hands at any time.

8. Do not wash the high-voltage components or electrical appliance compartment of the vehicle with water.

9. Do not artificially damage the high-voltage components of the vehicle.

Test safety requirements

1. All levels of maintenance and pre-inspection of pure electric vehicles are in a live and startable status, and the pre-inspection must be carried out by professionals.

2. Before the vehicle is powered on, make sure that no other personnel are carrying out maintenance and that the parking brake is applied and the gearshift lever is in neutral position.

3. After the vehicle is powered on, hang warning signs such as "Do Not Operate without Authorization" in the steering wheel area.

4. Before vehicle testing, diagnosis and completion inspection, carry out insulation test on insulating gloves. Do not use damaged insulating gloves. Only use the test instrument after confirming it is in good condition, so as to avoid high voltage accidents caused by false values output by faulty instruments.

5. Do not directly touch the orange wiring harnesses, high-voltage connectors or highvoltage components with bare hands.

6. Do not touch the terminals in high-voltage cable connectors with fingers, metal ends of small tools or iron bars.

7. When measuring the voltage of high-voltage terminal with a multimeter, do not touch the probe conductor by hand.

### Maintenance safety requirements

1. Before vehicle maintenance, make sure that the vehicle is in the maintenance area and set warning signs of "Danger! High Voltage" and "No Entry". Do not allow any nonmaintenance personnel to enter this area. Ensure that warning signs are removed by maintenance personnel only.

2. Before vehicle maintenance, check that the high-voltage power is disconnected.

3. During vehicle maintenance, record the number of all parts removed, and place these parts in the part tray in a clean and visible area. During re-installation, make sure that all parts are installed in place without surplus or missing parts to prevent small components such as bolts from falling into any highvoltage components.

4. During vehicle maintenance, use a special insulation plug cap or insulating tape to insulate the positive and negative connectors of cables of removed highvoltage components.

### Maintenance method

Vehicle maintenance plan

The maintenance of the vehicle shall be carried out as planned to ensure driving stability and reduce fault for safe and economical driving. Generally, the maintenance of vehicle shall be carried out at intervals specified in the maintenance schedule according to the odometer reading or time interval, whichever comes first. Overdue maintenance items should also be implemented at the same intervals.

Some items in the maintenance plan may need to be carried out more frequently if the vehicle is operated mainly under one or more of the following special conditions:

Road conditions

Driving on rough, muddy or snowy roads.
Driving on dusty roads.

Driving conditions

The vehicle is used to tow a camping trailer or a roof bracket is installed on the vehicle. The vehicle is driven within 8 km repeatedly and driven in an environment with temperature below zero. The vehicle is driven in long-term idling and/or low-speed long-distance driving conditions. The examples include police cars, taxis, or vehicles carrying goods.

Inspection of chassis fixing bolts and nuts

### A Caution:

The brake pad comprises substances that meet the Chinese standard, but it will be harmful to health if their dust is inhaled frequently. – It is required to use the vacuum cleaner to clean the brake assembly, instead of a suction hose or brush.

1. Remove the front brake pad assembly. Refer to Installation and Removal of Front Brake Pad Assembly

If the thickness of brake pad is less than the service limit, replace the whole set of brake pad.

### Inspection of front brake disc End face runout

1. Remove the front brake pad assembly. Refer to Installation and Removal of Front Brake Pad Assembly

2. Check whether the brake disc surface is damaged or cracked, thoroughly clean the brake disc and remove all rust.

![](images/57298356f9ef1b4dd0a283daa8fc01845bfd8ccd02c3af0bebe692187eb78c01.webp)

3. Install the dial indicator base on the body, and install the dial indicator measuring probe in place so that it is in contact with the friction surface of brake disc at 90° and is 10 mm away from the outer edge of brake disc.

4. Rotate the brake disc until the reading of dial indicator reaches the minimum, and then zero the dial indicator.

5. Rotate the brake disc until the reading of the dial indicator reaches the maximum, make a mark, and record the end face runout.

6. If the end face runout of brake disc exceeds the service limit of 0.08 mm, repair the brake disc with an on-board brake lathe.

Standard thickness of brake disc: 25 mm Maximum service limit of brake disc: 23 mm

### A Caution:

If the brake disc exceeds the service limit, replace it.

1. Remove the front brake pad assembly. Refer to Installation and Removal of Front Brake Pad Assembly

![](images/e4dce355e7a12439025e5d2e59387cc2158cf8e692b74fde5ee63daf2331a9e4.webp)

2. Use a micrometer to measure the thickness of brake disc at 8 points 10 mm away from the outer edge of brake disc and at the intervals of about 45°

Standard thickness of brake disc: 25 mm Maximum service limit of brake disc: 23 mm Parallelism of brake disc: max. 0.05 mm

### A Caution:

If the minimum measured value is less than the maximum service limit, replace the brake disc. If the parallelism of the brake disc exceeds the service limit, repair the brake disc with an on-board brake lathe.

### Reminder:

The brake pad is composed of toxic substances, so frequent inhalation of its dust will be harmful to your health.

Avoid inhaling brake pad dust.
Be sure to use the vacuum cleaner to clean the brake assembly, instead of a suction hose or brush.

Standard: 6.5 mm Service limit: 2 mm

### Inspection of rear brake disc Test

1. Vibration

a. Remove the rear brake pad assembly. Refer to Installation and Removal of Rear Brake Pad Assembly

b. Check the brake disc surface for damage or cracking. Thoroughly clean the brake disc and remove all rust.

c. Install appropriate flat washers and wheel nuts. Tighten the nut to the specified torque.

Tightening torque: 120±5 N•m d. Place the dial indicator against the brake disc, measure the vibration at 10 mm from the outer edge of the brake disc, and rotate the brake disc to observe the reading of the dial indicator pointer.

2. Thickness

![](images/f9b1f1e5e9b218f502115a8c32a8decb161af56060f526069a1c2a78423dea5c.webp)

a. Use a micrometer to measure the thickness of the brake disc at 8 points 10 mm away from the outer edge of the brake disc and at the intervals of about 45° If the minimum measured value is less than the maximum service limit, replace the brake disc.
