b. If the minimum measured value is less than the maximum service limit, replace the brake disc.
c. If the parallelism of the brake disc exceeds the service limit, repair the brake disc with an on-board brake lathe.

A Caution:

If the parallelism of the brake disc exceeds the re-service limit, replace the brake disc.

### Inspection of steering wheel

![](images/ca1341aa9f3f65cac1a2bd2cba3cdc0d6e2d11ae3392901f92a09ecd2f24191b.webp)

1. Check the steering wheel. a. Hold the steering wheel and shake it up, down, left, and right to check whether it is swinging or loose. b. With the vehicle powered up (OK), check whether the steering wheel is difficult to turn. If so, repair the steering system.

![](images/2b96ec4bf8eac52c065f24dfbae76aefda9704bff5e3cd10f5f6f2823f1a64cd.webp)

2. Check the free clearance of steering wheel.

a. Position the front wheels for driving in a straight line.
b. Power off the vehicle.
c. Mark the top of the steering wheel.
d. Place a ruler against the top of the steering wheel.
e. Measure the maximum distance to which the steering wheel can turn left under the condition that front wheels do not rotate.
f. Turn the steering wheel back to its original position.
g. Measure the maximum distance to which the steering wheel can turn right under the condition that front wheels do not rotate.
h. If the sum of the maximum left and right distances is not greater than 30 mm, the free stroke of the steering wheel is normal; otherwise, check the steering system.

### ? Reminder:

If the caster angle and inclination angle of the front wheel kingpin are not within the specified range, check suspension components for bending or damage. If the suspension components are bent or damaged, replace the damaged components. Do not try to repair them by tapping or other methods.

If camber angles of front and rear wheels are not within the specified range, check suspension components for bending or damage. If the suspension components are bent or damaged, replace the damaged components. Do not try to repair them by tapping or other methods.

– If the front wheel toe-in is correct, but the steering angle is not within the specified range or the left inner steering angle is different from the right one, check suspension components for bending or damage. If the suspension components are bent or damaged, replace the damaged components. Do not try to repair them by tapping or other methods.

The suspension device can be used to adjust the front wheel toe-in and rear wheel toe-in.

### Wheel alignment parameter value

![](images/2e699db83396739356b493ac30241990a184e46647d32daaa791da7eb068595c.webp)

Toe-in angle of front wheel

### A Caution:

In this model, only the toe-in value of the front wheel can be adjusted through the steering rod, and other parameters of wheel alignment cannot be adjusted.

1. Inspection before four-wheel alignment:

a. Release the parking brake to avoid incorrect measurement.
b. Make sure that the suspension device is not changed.
c. Make sure that the 4 tires are of the same specification, and that the tire pressure is within the specified range.
d. Make sure that there are no people or extra loads in the vehicle.
e. Check whether each fixing point of suspension is loose and deformed, and check the clearance of suspension ball heads to ensure it is not too large.
f. Check the wheels for vibration.
g. Check to confirm that both sides of the vehicle are level with each other.
h. The steering wheel alignment tolerance is 0° ±0.2
i. Carry out a dynamic balance test on wheels, and install them back on the vehicle after the test.
j. Make the wheels bounce up and down several times to stabilize the suspension.
k. The test bench is in normal condition.
l. Adjust the rear wheels first and then the front wheels.

2. Test:

a. Check the wheel alignment according to the operating instructions of the fourwheel aligner.

![](images/f9f845317670df1c82d37ac989b4d3369efcfd0610ec9b251ac8e9cf741db592.webp)

3. Adjust the front wheel toe-in. a. Loosen the steering link lock nut. b. Place 1 open-end wrench at the hexagonal position of the steering links, and adjust the front wheel toe-in to the standard value by rotating the left or right link. Front wheel toe-in value: 1.3±1.82mm c. Tighten the lock nut. Tightening torque: 70 N•m

### Reminder:

The adjustment methods of the rear left and rear right wheel total toe-ins are the same.

![](images/37ea7fe67f3ad22ec3ae7134b2978d65b922a827b1ca7ef38a1977139b3f42e8.webp)

4. Adjustment of rear wheel toe-in

? Reminder:

The adjustment methods of the rear left and rear right wheel total toe-ins are the same.

a. Fix the eccentric bolt with a tool.
b. Loosen the lock nut.
c. Rotate the rear wheel toe-in adjusting eccentric bolt until the toe-in is correct. Rear wheel toe-in value: 1.56±3.56mm
d. After adjustment, fix the eccentric bolt and tighten the lock nut. Tightening torque: 70 N•m

### A Caution:

The connection points of camber
eccentric bolts can only be installed and removed once after sales. After this, nuts need to be replaced with new ones. Bolts and gaskets should be replaced as needed. In case of rust, it is
recommended to replace them with new ones.
Make sure that the gasket and eccentric bolt gasket are both properly seated in the limit groove.

![](images/40d587af336dad64ecddeb095e107c23b51ba084b2b4964729f3a777d3577672.webp)

5. Adjustment of rear wheel camber angle.

? Reminder:

The adjustment methods of the rear left and rear right wheel camber angles are the same.

a. Fix the eccentric bolt with a tool.
b. Loosen the lock nut.
c. Rotate the eccentric bolt for adjusting the rear wheel camber angle until the camber angle is correct. Rear wheel camber angle: -1.07±0.5

d. After adjustment, fix the eccentric bolt and tighten the lock nut. Tightening torque: 70 N•m

### A Caution:

The connecting points of camber
eccentric bolts can only be removed and installed twice after sales. After this, nuts need to be replaced with new ones.
Bolts and gaskets should be replaced as needed. In case of rust, it is
recommended to replace them with new ones.
Make sure that the gasket and eccentric bolt gasket are both properly seated in the limit groove.

### i Reminder:

To ensure even tire wear and prolong the service life of tires, it is recommended to perform tire rotation according to the maintenance schedule. However, the most appropriate time for tire rotation depends on the driver's driving habits and road conditions. It is necessary to re-match and learn the tire pressure monitoring module after tire rotation. Refer to Tire pressure monitoring module matching

Front and rear tires bear different loads and experience varying degrees of wear. To prevent uneven wear, it is necessary to rotate tires regularly or as needed, thus extending their lifespan. One rotation every 5000-8000 km is recommended. The main purposes of tire rotation are as follows:

Ensure even tire wear and fatigue to improve stability and costeffectiveness. Check the condition of tires during rotation to find out the damage in time and prevent accidents. When rotating tires, make sure that steering tires are in the best condition to improve the vehicle stability and safety.

Cross tire rotation

1. Remove 4 wheel assemblies of the vehicle.
2. Move wheel 1 to the original installation position of wheel 4.
3. Move wheel 4 to the original installation position of wheel 2.
4. Move wheel 2 to the original installation position of wheel 3.
5. Move wheel 3 to the original installation position of wheel 1.

![](images/ecd93c6e95c474e76ee090523bacd23649f56712b820329c5dca041f31ded2d0.webp)

? Reminder:

The methods for the left and right sides are the same. Take the left one as an example. Make sure that the test paper is printed at 1:1 scale, with the dotted line box for left or right headlight cluster being ? Reminder: 430 mm × 350 mm. Please check that dimensions are correct after printing. Attach the test paper to the corresponding position box of the test screen. After use, put it in a folder or file bag, and properly keep it in the spare parts warehouse.

Preparation of test site

![](images/6a001b68548b3a549f3c8516dd3cdaf26cf4ad84821ad36709650e929b63ecdd.webp)

1. Make sure that the test site is flat and spacious, and avoid the influence of strong light irradiation on dimming.

2. Draw a straight line parallel to the test screen on the ground 3 m away from the test screen, draw the vehicle centerline on the ground, and make sure that the centerline is perpendicular to the 3 m line and the test screen.

Designation of letters in the figure:

![](images/6265c47c19d8bf061db8f1ee09a5573dfae4932af2358606c5d323ff7d22697e.webp)

Preparation of test vehicle

1. Check and make sure that there is no damage or deformation of the vehicle and around the headlights.

2. Make sure that the vehicle lubricating oil level and the coolant level meet the design requirements.

3. Make sure that the tire pressure meets the standard inflation pressure requirement.

4. Never place other articles in the vehicle, but be sure to place the tools delivered with the vehicle at the specified positions.

5. Have a person weighing 75 kg seated in the driver's seat (counterweight method is allowed if the weight is below 75 kg).

6. Place the vehicle on a horizontal plane and shake the vehicle body from side to side to make the chassis suspension of the vehicle stay in a stable state.

### Inspection and adjustment of headlight dimming function

7. For a vehicle equipped with a dimmer switch, turn the headlight adjustment switch to "0" position before dimming; for a vehicle without a dimmer switch (i.e. automatic dimming), check whether the light MIL on the instrument panel cluster illuminates before dimming. If it illuminates or flashes, conduct repair, make a record and provide feedback; if it does not illuminate or flash, complete initialization with the VDS.

![](images/570716499dd2eba411a0b3a3d1ad535e6453c65feeba11eddd642ea7f07dbbdc.webp)

8. Connect the VDS and enter the diagnostic system interface.

9. Power on the vehicle.

10. Go to: Model diagnosis/(corresponding model code)/Body module/Headlight adjustment unit/Headlight initialization.

Test steps

> ⚠️ **Внимание:** 
> – For a model with joint adjustment of high and low beams, only low beams need to be adjusted. There are two light patterns of low beams, namely 1 ）= and " ". The lower inflection point of cut-off line is taken as the light pattern center of low beams, while the brightest spot is taken as the light pattern center of high beams.
> – If low beams need to be shielded for adjusting high beams, headlight surfaces cannot be directly shielded or the shielding time cannot exceed 2 minutes as headlight covers are made of plastic, so as to avoid gathering of heat that may cause burn-out of headlight covers.
> – During light adjustment, observe beam positions while rotating the adjusting bolt. Make proper adjustment at one time whenever possible. Refrain from continuous and prolonged rotation of the adjusting bolt with an electric screwdriver to prevent need for subsequent readjustment caused by excessive adjustment. Adjust the light inflection point to the test box center whenever possible.
>
> 1. Attach the dimming test paper of the corresponding model to the position box (for a wall, it is recommended to use a paper
>
> tape; for a whiteboard, it is recommended to use a magnet).
>
> 2. Park the vehicle in front of the 3 m line, that is, the low beam reference center (the intersection point between the low beam bulb axis and the light cover) is 3 m away from the test screen. In addition, keep the vehicle centerline overlapping with the vehicle centerline drawn on the ground and vertically aligned with the centerline on the test wall.
>
> 3. Start the vehicle and turn on headlights.
>
> 4. Check whether the light pattern centers of headlights are in the corresponding test boxes. If so, headlights are normal. If not, adjust headlights.
>
> ![](images/529e6f79cc45928450c19018e763e86453701b21e276868f51c4c70990c93d87.webp)
>
> 5. Adjust the headlight cluster assembly.

### i Reminder:

The adjustment method of left headlight cluster assembly is the same as the right one. Take the left one as an example.

a. Adjust the light source in horizontal direction. b. Adjust the light source in vertical direction.

Light sources mentioned above refer to irradiation sources of headlight cluster assemblies.

![](images/8deccad91d052a5429c93e259c06661d0419ed94824617b2791618313c9b9c92.webp)

### Inspection of EPS

![](images/8112015aaa69e849dcfa9735c0bfc808d4b782d999d327993d1036e358d8bb52.webp)

1. Check the vehicle modules. a. Connect the VDS and check the vehicle modules for software update. If any, update the software. b. Check the vehicle modules for DTCs. If any, clear the DTCs. c. Read the DTC again. If DTC still exists, eliminate the fault.

### Inspection of front wiper blade

1. Enter the Infotainment system → Vehicle health → Maintenance interface to enable front wiper maintenance.

![](images/9f81e5d4ee6f7f9877bcc62bece73b738d903bacda71f1fc464afa05ad6f292b.webp)

2. Grasp the upper end of the wiper arm, carefully lift the wiper arm and blade assembly, and check for aging, cracking, poor wiping, water film or abnormal sound. ### ? Caution:

If the coolant is hot, wait for the coolant to cool down before operating. Otherwise, the high temperature and high pressure coolant will be sprayed out, resulting in serious personal injury.

### Discharge

1. Remove the front bumper assembly See Installation and Removal of Front Bumper Assembly

![](images/feaf3a3e2ee710a22a6af275372df9c0e610b3a4f470e821393850ac239c4de4.webp)

2. Open the expansion tank cover.

3. Loosen 7 fixing clamp, detach the cooling pipe assembly from the motor radiator assembly l, and discharge the coolant.

![](images/ba20e0ec84b8eca5cc59a4206f57c663337aa71b4af5fb93ba4c16d5c3f2f84f.webp)
Filling

A Caution:

Collect the coolant in the collecting container at the junction between the cooling pipe assembly and the motor radiator assembly until the coolant is drained.

![](images/64869a18a1c5b84acc509a283e24b00e48092c8485a0dd004101c0151d7033ae.webp)

1. Install cooling pipe assembly 1 to its original position.

![](images/bcdf283b70ec21214cfe78b066ae512478eddade0bb5dc13c24504dd137dd985.webp)

2. Fill the coolant between the "MAX" and "MIN" markings in the expansion tank assembly I, and install the expansion tank cap.

### A Caution:

Observe the coolant level in
the expansion tank assembly I. If the coolant is lower than the "Min" mark, add coolant until it reaches between the "Max" and "Min" marks.
Do not dilute the coolant at will, coolant do not reuse, mixed use, do not allow to replace different colors of coolant.
Coolant protects against frost, corrosion and scaling, and also increases boiling point, so coolant must be filled
standardly.
Coolant must be recovered in
accordance with the relevant national regulations.

### A Caution:

When removing the brake tube or intelligent power braking system, the brake fluid must be drained and filled. Before draining, use VDS to confirm that the braking system has no fault code. The brake fluid has a strong corrosive effect on the paint. If it is accidentally splashed on the
paint of the vehicle body, it must be cleaned with a rag as soon as possible.
– Avoid oil contact with skin. If it is accidentally splashed into the eyes, immediately rinse with plenty of water and seek medical attention as soon as possible. Do not discharge the oil at will, and recycle it according to local regulations. After completion, use VDS to check that the braking system has no fault code.

### Reminder:

The method for draining the brake fluid of the front and rear wheels is the same. Take the left rear side as an example.

![](images/39453d38a41fdbad31e4772cc4deb780f4ae055d20b5c88832563e5e1c23b609.webp)

1. Remove the bleed bolt cover.

2. Connect the brake fluid collection container to the exhaust screw and loosen the exhaust screw.

3. Depress brake pedal, and drain the brake fluid.

Filling

### A Caution:

Check whether there is dirt in the brake fluid reservoir before filling. Do not refill used brake fluid, and fill brake fluid of the same specificatio

### A Caution:

Ensure that the brake fluid level is within the specified range after filling.

1. Open the brake fluid reservoir filler cap and fill the brake fluid.

![](images/e2055561c94cc0d4e54ad6c94550330f99fd92d99b0e483fd48b6517ac9b48e6.webp)

2. Loosen the exhaust screw, slowly depress the brake pedal to the bottom, then loosen the pedal, repeat every 2-3 seconds until the new brake fluid is discharged from the exhaust screw.

3. Depress the brake pedal, and tighten the exhaust screw. 4. Perform the same operation for the other 3 wheels according to this method. 5. Air discharge of brake system See Air Discharge of Brake System

6. Install the bleed bolt cover.

### ? Caution:

Before replacing the gear oil, make sure that the vehicle has been driven for more than 3 km, which is conducive to completely discharging the gear oil.

![](images/95866914c7d7ac6f18b49ffedd66a569af8480503caac841be267f832c36df39.webp)

If the vehicle is overheated, wait until the vehicle cools down to near room temperature, otherwise there is a risk of scalding.

Discharge the Gear Oil

![](images/47113afb9d1891a2cad582fa32544e7df181a64d64c1c3cafe0c5c8e565426b6.webp)

### Refill the Gear Oil

1. Lift the vehicle, and make sure the vehicle is level.

2. Remove the front subframe mudguard assembly. See Installation and Removal of Front Subframe Mudguard

3. Remove 1 oil filler plug. Tightening torque: 37±2N•m

### A Caution:

Place the collection container below the plug in advance.
Be careful when unscrewing the plug to avoid oil spilling out of the collecting container.

4. Remove 1 oil drain plug, drain clean gear oil, and then install the oil drain plug.

Tightening torque: 50± 3N•m

### A Caution:

Before installing the screw plug, clean its threads and contact surface. The discharged oil must be collected and treated according to the local laws and regulations. It is forbidden to discharge or discard the oil without permission.

1. Fill the gear oil in the oil filling plug hole.

Model: Castrol BOT384 or equivalent gear oil.
Amount: 0.45±0.05L

![](images/057ec98eda31fb3ecf44eed5d470c3d98811acde24b5e6cbb7a3357223f0fbb2.webp)

2. Install the oil fill plug. Tightening torque: 37±2N•m

3. Install in the reverse order of removal.

### A Caution:

The power battery is a dangerous high voltage product. The maintenance personnel must pay attention to the following precautions during removal and installation:

The connection points indicated with yellow line or parts with high voltage signs of the power battery may only be dismantled by personnel without professional training.

When the power battery is removed, the socket must be covered with insulation protection.

Power battery output socket must be insulated to protect it from foreign objects which may cause the electric shock;

During the removal, pay attention that the sampling wire must not be pulled violently and bent excessively to prevent the signal wire from being damaged;

Pay attention to the identification of parts during power battery disassembly to avoid omission or incorrect installation;

During the removal and installation, the power battery must be prevented from the violent removal, dropping, collision, module tilting, artificial short circuit and other abnormal operations; it can only be removed by non-professional workers.

Power battery is a high voltage device, and improper operation may easily cause the personal injury or death. Please refer to this disassembly & assembly specification for all procedures and precautions.

Tighten the screws with professional tools according to the designed torque; the bolts must be marked for fastening after installation.

### Systems Manual Overview

The power battery pack is mainly composed of executive unit (BASU), BIC, and battery sampling line, which are placed inside the battery pack.

The main functions of BASU include charge and discharge management, contactor control, power control, abnormal battery state alarm and protection, SOC/SOH calculation, communication function, current sampling function, total voltage sampling, contactor sintering detection, leakage detection, etc.

The main functions of the BIC include cell voltage sampling, battery temperature sampling, and battery equalization.

The main function of the power battery sampling line is to connect BASU and BIC to realize communication and information exchange.

TBYD Dolphin is equipped with two power battery pack, the model of version 400 km of the battery pack is P94, and the model of version 300 km of the battery pack is P95.

### ? Warning:

– When repairing the high voltage system (the high voltage system harnesses are identified by orange on the vehicle), wear insulation protection equipment, including insulating gloves, insulating shoes and masks, and power down the high voltage system of the vehicle. – To avoid the personal injury, only the professionals may remove the power battery. – Do not touch or operate the power battery without appropriate protective equipment. Please switch the vehicle power supply to OFF position before operation.
– Remove the battery according to the process.
During the removal, pay attention to the high voltage warning signs on the power battery and the vehicle.
During the removal, do not damage the parts with locking function.
During the removal, properly protect the power battery.

### Removal

1. Adjust the driver and front passenger seat assemblies to the foremost position.
2. Power off the low voltage electrical system. See Power-off and Power-on of Low Voltage Electrical System
3. Power off the high voltage electrical system. See Power-off and power-on of highvoltage electrical system
4. Discharge the refrigerant. See Refrigerant Recovery and Refueling
5. Remove the front subframe mudguard assembly. See Installation and Removal of Front Subframe Mudguard
6. Disconnect 1 connector of front compartment harness.

![](images/ab2f0bdb27966152127c50de412dda29a7a540dbc8facdb49980fbfe0c4e77a3.webp)

![](images/bdeea06655e37f6f78bce2777e6c62b61c37039566e54e7531f781a33752380d.webp)

7. Disconnect 2 connector of front compartment harness.

8. Remove 1 fixing bolt and detach the compressor suction pipe assembly 3 from the power battery pack.

Tightening torque: xxxN•m

### A Caution:

Remove the A/C pipeline involving the O-rings. Install new O-rings after each removal. Apply compressor lubricating oil to the new O-rings before installation. After removing the components of the A/C system, all components need to be sealed to prevent foreign matters such as dust and impurities from entering the A/C system and causing abnormalities.

![](images/86e5548222384b6d5286ce3a0b1591bcace5e19a76354113a3c8aa7584dcf6d2.webp)

9. Remove 2 fixing bolts of high voltage harness bracket.

Tightening torque: xxxN•m

10. Remove 2 fixing bolts and disconnect the high voltage connector and the power battery pack.

Tightening torque: xxxN•m

### A Caution:

After the high voltage components are disassembled, they must be sealed and insulated to prevent dust and impurities from entering or accidentally touching the high voltage terminals.

![](images/35ef887c9df889ea0178a599fb0934400bb689d50bbee9d9d35c941493abc6db.webp)

11. Remove fixing bolt, and take out the battery pack ground harness. Tightening torque: xxxN•m

12. Support the power battery with the lifting equipment of the liftable platform.

a. Place the lifting equipment of the liftable platform just below the power battery pack.
b. Raise the lift platform slowly to ensure that the lifting equipment holds the power battery pack firmly.
c. Do not allow the lift platform to obscure the power battery pack fixing bolt.

> ⚠️ **Внимание:** 
> The power battery assembly must be firmly supported to prevent personal injury and damage to the power battery assembly caused by falling power battery assembly.

### A Caution:

Place soft supports materials (such as thick wooden frames, rubber pads) on the lifting equipment of the liftable platform to prevent lift platform from damaging the power battery assembly.

![](images/c241aec3cf917fe9b740a575c012b09a562ebbdd0eaa056dafb95478e3851174.webp)

![](images/22969f2fabc26d7febc270b775d96993a18458323b1f3565218fcaac62a517d1.webp)

13. Use a plastic crow plate to remove 2 carpet blanking covers.

14. Remove 2 fixing bolts of the power battery pack.

Tightening torque: 6N m

15. Remove 10 fixing bolts of the battery pack, and adjust the battery pack disassembly tool to lower the power battery pack slowly.

Tightening torque: 135N m

### A Caution:

When removing the power battery assembly, more than one people is needed to cooperate with each other. When lowering the power battery assembly, observe whether there is interference with the body. After removing the power battery assembly, seal all connectors to prevent the dust and impurities from entering and causing pollution, blockage or the risk of electric shock when touching the high voltage connector by mistake.

Installation

### A Caution:

Pay attention to standardized operation when installing the lifting power battery assembly. Slowly lift the power battery assembly and observe whether there is interference with the body. Pay attention to align the mounting hole of the adjusting bolt with the mounting hole of the

### ? Caution:

vehicle body. Screw in 14 fixing bolts in sequence and tighten them according to the specified torque.

1. Install in the reverse order of removal.

2. After installation, fill in the refrigerant. See Refrigerant Recovery and Refueling

3. Power on the vehicle high voltage system. See Power-off and power-on of highvoltage electrical system

4. Power on the low voltage electrical system. See Power-off and Power-on of Low Voltage Electrical System

A Caution:

Uncover the front drive electric assembly package II side. Each time the left cover of the integrated intelligent front drive assembly is removed, the operation must be standardized. The bolts must be removed from the outside to the inside.

### Installation

1. Install in the reverse order of removal.

2. After installation, fill in the coolant. See Coolant Discharging and Filling

3. After installation, fill in the refrigerant. See Refrigerant Recovery and Refueling

### A Caution:

Since the intelligent front drive assembly is integrated with the power domain control module and front drive motor control module, perform the following calibrations 1-5 when replacing the electronic control, and perform calibration 5 only when replacing the drive motor.

![](images/600daeab7970909fad002a30fd6e84e6c6111a4f0bc14f0fcd65682569c1f4dd.webp)

1. Immobilizer matching (password clearing and programming): a. Place the key at the immobilizer RF card reader.

b. Connect the VDS and enter the diagnostic system interface.

c. Select "Dolphin" model.

d. Select "Special diagnosis function".

e. Tap "Immobilizer matching".

f. Tap "Clear password of motor control unit", and the VDS displays that the password is cleared successfully.

g. Enter immobilizer matching interface again, select "Motor control unit programming", and tap "Execute", with "Programming successful" displayed.

2. Inclination calibration a. Power on the vehicle and stop it stably to a horizontal position.

![](images/7cf9ba0fe845ec7f47c0154908141d4b2f9f3c0bbe0afa421119f0bfd81acf07.webp)

b. Connect the VDS and enter the diagnostic system interface.

c. Select "Dolphin" model.

d. Select "Power domain control unit".

e. Select "Inclination calibration".

f. Manually conduct inclination calibration. g. Read the data flow, and VDS displays "Calibrated" for "Inclination calibration information/Calibration or not".

3. Vehicle VIN writing and reading

![](images/d1d19edbd2d9ad60ed633e4d997d264964858f462efa13136be37a0628da57b5.webp)

a. Power on the vehicle.
b. Connect the VDS and enter the diagnostic system interface.

c. Select "Dolphin" model.

d. Select "Power domain control unit".

e. Vehicle VIN writing and reading

f. Tap "Vehicle VIN writing".
g. Identify the vehicle VIN and check that the read VIN is consistent with the real vehicle VIN.
h. Return to the previous page "VIN writing" and tap "Run".

![](images/af5ff36746a226b1c1d1f5fd2e8b7dfefe3a0552ef0ead78f0afc0ff130cf5cc.webp)

i. VDS displays that the writing is successful, and the identified VIN is consistent with the vehicle VIN. j. Read the data flow, and the feedback value of "VIN written or not" is "Written".

4. Cruise configuration calibration

a. Power on the vehicle.
b. Connect the VDS and enter the diagnostic system interface.
c. Select "Dolphin" model.
d. Select "Power domain control unit" and "Cruise configuration calibration".
e. Select "Cruise control" or "Adaptive cruise control" based on the model.
f. Select "Activate calibration".

5. Zero-position calibration

### A Caution:

When the drive motor controller or drive motor is replaced separately, zero calibration is required. When replacing the assembly, zero calibration is not required. After replacing the drive motor control module or drive motor separately, use VDS to perform the zero calibration according to the following steps: Set the vehicle to ON, or park the vehicle by switching to gear P, connect and start the diagnostic equipment, and select the "Dolphin" model as follows.

a. Record the motor zeroposition barcode (case sensitive).

![](images/c48388ba9a468271aa57536bda2729973d641f3a35dc43290ccc5bdec904bef7.webp)

b. Connect the VDS and enter the diagnostic system interface.

c. Select "Front drive motor control unit".

d. Tap "Motor Zero-position Calibration".

e. Properly enter the motor zero-position barcode and tap "Confirm". If the barcode is confirmed, "Operation succeeded" will be displayed; if the barcode is wrong, "Negative response" will be displayed.

f. Power off and restart the vehicle. After successful calibration, check whether the zero-position calibration is successful by VDS data flow reading (i.e. whether the latest zero-position value is the same as the current motor barcode zero-position value).

### Installation and Removal of the Left Differential Oil Seal Removal

1. Discharge the differential mechanism gear oil. See Gear Oil Replacement

![](images/2b625d09a047c6e24040e8d633c9a6822551b21081e8c30c9bff8719aec79766.webp)

2. Remove the left front drive half shaft assembly. See Installation and Removal of Left Front Drive Half Shaft Assembly

3. Carefully remove the left differential oil seal.

### A Caution:

When removing the oil seal, special care must be taken not to scratch the reducer housing.
The differential oil seal is not reusable and needs to be installed with a new
differential oil seal.

Installation

1. Install the differential oil seal with the special tool (Tool Name: half shaft oil seal installation tool; Material No. 13461863-00). See "Special Tools Manual"

### A Caution:

Before installing the differential oil seal, clean the differential oil seal base and the new differential oil seal.
Apply a thin layer of differential
lubricating oil to the outer wall of the
differential oil seal before installation. When installing the differential oil seal, be careful to prevent installing it at an angle.
After the differential oil seal is installed, it is necessary to check and ensure that it is installed in place.

Installation

2. Remove the right front drive half shaft assembly. See Installation and Removal of Right Front Drive Half Shaft Assembly

3. Carefully remove the right differential oil seal.

### A Caution:

When removing the oil seal, special care must be taken not to scratch the reducer housing.
The differential oil seal is not reusable and needs to be installed with a new
differential oil seal.

1. Install the differential oil seal with the special tool (Tool Name: half shaft oil seal installation tool; Material No. 13461863-00). See "Special Tools Manual"

### A Caution:

After replacement with the new repair kit for drive MCU assembly, calibrate the VTOL discharging function of the vehicle with the VDS. Before calibration, please check the VDS software for the latest version.

![](images/18e781d7a474031901cad51b403e40d955eb579b66ea38b5d3be99ab1bbbd193.webp)

1. Connect the vehicle OBD interface with VDS. Refer to VDS User Manual

0 Reminder:

The OBD interface is located in the lower right corner of the lower right shield of the instrument panel.

2. With the charging connector not connected, power on the vehicle to "OK", go to the "Vehicle Diagnosis System" interface and select the vehicle model.

3. After scanning the vehicle module, enter the "On-board Charger" diagnosis interface.

4. In the diagnosis interface, select "Calibration".

5. Select "VTOL Discharge".

6. After entering the interface, select "No VTOL Discharge" according to the configuration table. If there is no VTOL function, mark it as "No VTOL Discharge".

7. Tap "Discharge Frequency and Voltage" and select the corresponding discharge voltage and frequency according to the local power grid specifications.

8. After successful calibration, the calibration results can be read back through the right interface.

### A Caution:

The high voltage system harnesses are identified in orange color on the vehicle. Before performing maintenance work of the high voltage system, wear insulation protection equipment, including insulating gloves, insulating shoes and mask.
The parts with the high voltage
identification must not be disassembled without the professional training personnel. The high voltage system harness must not be bent during removal, otherwise the harness will be damaged.
If the high voltage system harness is
damaged, aged or cracked, replace it with a new one.

Systems Manual System Overview

New energy vehicles high voltage harness is a key component of high voltage electrical system, which provides a guarantee for the reliable and safe operation of new energy vehicles. It carries connection between the internal and external harness of electric vehicles, distributes power through the power distribution box, transmits electric energy efficiently with high quality, shields external signal interference and other functions. It is the neural network of the high voltage system of new energy vehicles, connecting all high voltage electronic components and transmitting power and data, which is extremely important for new energy vehicles.

High current: new energy vehicles high voltage harness as the main energy transmission channel, to withstand high current, DC bus rated current can reach more than 200 A.

Sealing: Due to the high voltage and high current characteristics of the high voltage harness, there are also high requirements for the sealing of the harness, which generally requires water and dust resistance tests and air tightness tests. If the sealing is not good, the moisture or water ingress occurs, resulting in extremely rapid ageing or damage to the wire and connection parts. If the sealing performance of the connector part is poor, the insulation resistance will be reduced and the insulation fault will be reported.

Heat resistance: because the highvoltage harness undergoes the high current for a long time, with high power and Joule effect of a lot of heat, the high voltage harness wire temperature rating generally reaches 125 。 C (150 C) and the terminal temperature generally reaches 140 0 C

When repairing the high voltage system (the high voltage system harnesses are identified by orange on the vehicle), wear insulation protection equipment, including insulating gloves, insulating shoes and masks, and power down the high voltage system of the vehicle.

### Removal

1. Power off the low-voltage electrical system. Refer to Power-off and power-on of lowvoltage electrical system

2. Powering high-voltage electrical system off and on Refer to Power-off and power-on of high-voltage electrical system

3. Remove the front subframe mudguard assembly. Refer to Installation and Removal of Front Subframe Mudguard

4. Remove the front subframe rear anticollision bar. Refer to Removal and installation of front subframe rear anticollision bar

![](images/d8004c04b933fe29a3ae3e8aabfc5155b2aba901ab7c51c6adffa1efd7461f18.webp)

5. Remove 2 fixing bolts of the high-voltage distribution wiring harness subassembly. Tightening torque: 9 N•m

6. Remove 2 fixing bolts to detach the high-voltage distribution wiring harness subassembly from the high-voltage battery pack and take it out.

Tightening torque: 5 N•m

A Caution:

After the high voltage components are disassembled, they must be sealed and insulated to prevent dust and impurities from entering or accidentally touching the high voltage terminals.

### A Caution:

The high voltage system harnesses are identified in orange color on the vehicle. Before performing maintenance work of the high voltage system, wear insulation protection equipment, including insulating gloves, insulating shoes and mask.

The parts with the high voltage identification must not be disassembled without the professional training personnel.

The integrated AC/DC charging vehicle socket subassembly must not be bent when removing, otherwise the harness will be damaged.

If the integrated AC/DC charging vehicle socket sub-assembly is damaged, aged or cracked, replace it with a new one.

Visually check the plastic insulation shell of charging port for the hot melting deformation, and replace the part if there is any thermal deformation.

Visually check the charging port and terminal for the foreign matters, discharge the foreign matters with high-pressure air gun and replace the charging port and terminal of which the foreign matters affect the normal operation.

Visually check whether the leaf spring and the bottom of charging port are blackened, and replace the blackened ones.

Visually check whether the leaf spring and bottom of charging port become yellow. If so, remove right front wheel assembly and right front mud guard, to check whether the cable at the rear of charging port is burnt and deformed (with the auxiliary lighting). Replace the leaf spring which turns yellow and the outer layer of cable turns black.

### Systems Manual Overview

The external charging gun is connected to the integrated AC/DC charging vehicle socket subassembly. The charging current of the charging gun flows through the high voltage harness to the drive motor control module assembly, and then is converted by the drive motor control module assembly (charger) to the power battery pack through the high voltage distribution harness sub-assembly for charging.

### A Caution:

To avoid personal injury, do not remove the filler cap until the coolant has cooled down completely. Otherwise, boiling liquid and steam may eject under pressure because the filler cap is opened too early.

Do not dilute the coolant at will. The coolant cannot be reused or mixed. Coolant of different colors cannot be changed.

Do not add coolant with inconsistent boiling point and freezing point at will. Instead, use coolant that conforms to the specified model of the vehicle. Alcohol or methanol coolant or water alone cannot be used as coolant liquid for cooling system. The cooling system may fail.

Observe the "MAX" and "MIN" markings of the coolant reservoir. If the coolant reservoir level is lower than the "MIN" marking, check the cooling system for leakage.

### System descriptions Overview

The cooling system consists of motor coolant pump, motor radiator assembly I, electronic fan assembly I, expansion tank assembly I, coolant pipeline and other components.

The cooling system mainly relies on the motor coolant pump to drive the coolant to circulate in the coolant pipeline, take away the heat generated by the integrated front drive assembly, and cool down the system through physical processes such as heat exchange in the radiator. When the coolant reaches a certain temperature, the electronic fan starts to work to maintain the integrated front drive assembly at the optimal temperature for operation.

### ? Caution:

The accelerator pedal is an integral part. Do not disassemble its internal parts. Do not touch the pin inside the plug when removing from the accelerator pedal. After removing from the accelerator pedal, it is necessary to prevent it from falling, bumping dust and waterproof treatment.

### System descriptions Overview

The accelerator pedal converts the driver's driving intention into an electronic signal through the electronic structure in the pedal, and transmits it to the vehicle control unit (ECU) through the bus. After calculation according to the vehicle conditions, the ECU reasonably adjusts the power system of the vehicle to achieve the driver's driving intention.

### Adjustment of accelerator pedal assembly Adjustment Procedure

1. Check if the accelerator pedal sensor and harness connector are connected properly, and install it in place in case of falling-off or looseness.

2. Check the accelerator pedal for damage or looseness. In case of breakage or deformation, replace the accelerator pedal; in case of looseness, tighten the fasteners to the specified torque.

3. Depress the accelerator pedal completely, release it, and confirm that it can return to the initial position within 400 ms. Otherwise, the accelerator pedal must be replaced.

### ? Caution:

While removing the mount, check whether the lifting device is firmly supported. Otherwise, the mount may be damaged or serious personal injury may occur. When removing the mount, use equipment to firmly support the powertrain, otherwise the vehicle may be damaged or serious personal injury may occur. If the mount cracks, ages, or loosens, please replace it with new ones, otherwise it will be difficult to ensure safe driving.

### Systems Manual Overview

The main function of mount assembly is to connect the powertrain with the front subframe assembly, which is used as supporting, and also reduces the vibration transmission of the powertrain when the powertrain works.

### ? Caution:

Lifting vehicles must be carried out
in accordance with standard operating procedures.
Wear safety helmet and safety shoes to prevent accidental injury when operating under the lifted vehicle.
After installing the front subframe, tighten the fixing bolt according to the standard torque.
Wheel alignment must be carried out after the removal and installation of the front sub-frame.

Overview

The front subframe is fixed on the body, and its main function is to install the powertrain, which provides the mounting surface for the steering gear, lower swing arm and stabilizer bar. It is an auxiliary support structure.

### A Caution:

Before removing the front subframe assembly, hoist the powertrain with the equipment. Taking out the front subframe assembly requires cooperations of several maintenance technicians.

### Removal

1. Remove the front subframe and powertrain. See Installation and Removal of Front Subframe and Powertrain

2. Remove the front stabilizer bar fitting assembly. See Installation and Removal of Front Stabilizer Bar Fitting Assembly

3. Remove the mechanical steering gear with tie rod assembly. See Installation and Removal of Mechanical Steering Gear With Tie Rod Assembly

![](images/2b62c7427d5801c183ae215f24c0ff7602996550e1fe357cf09942486041c426.webp)

5. Remove the front subframe assembly.

a. Remove 2 fixing nuts of the front subframe assembly. Tightening torque: 55± 5N•m
b. Remove 6 fixing bolts and take out the front subframe assembly. Tightening torque: 55± 5N•m

Installation

1. Install in the reverse order of removal.

Installation

1. Install it in the reverse order of removal.

### ? Warning:

After removing the lower swing arm assembly, check whether the rubber bushing is aged or damaged. Replace the lower swing arm assembly if it is aged or damaged. Do not repair it.

### A Caution:

Before installing the wheel, clean the mating surface of the brake disc and the inner surface of the wheel. Verify front wheel alignment. Adjust if necessary.

### Overview

The main function of the lower swing arm is to transfer the torque between the body and the wheel, keep the wheel moving within a certain range, and keep the lower swing arm moving along a certain trajectory.

### Removal

1. Remove the left front wheel assembly. See Installation and Removal of Wheel Assembly

2. Remove the front subframe mudguard assembly. See nstallation and Removal of Front Subframe Mudguard

![](images/f46e1e0656c20823a0e8ce36c054924382eea52cecd97fe8f326ca57cc48fce8.webp)

3. Remove the left front lower swing arm assembly and the fastener of the ball stud press assembly.

a. Remove 2 fixing nut. Tightening torque: 90N m
b. Remove fixing bolt. Tightening torque: 90N m

4. Remove the left front lower swing arm assembly.

a. Remove fixing nut, and take out 1 fixing bolt. Tightening torque: 200N m

b. Remove 1 fixing nut, take out 1 fixing bolt, and take out the left front lower swing arm assembly. Tightening torque: 200N m

### A Caution:

Take out the left front lower swing arm assembly with the assistance of another maintenance technician.

1. Install in the reverse order of removal.

2. Wheel alignment must be carried out after installation. See Wheel Alignment

### Removal

1. Remove the right front wheel assembly. See Installation and Removal of Wheel Assembly

2. Remove the front subframe mudguard assembly. See Installation and Removal of Front Subframe Mudguard

![](images/557ea75872980582a28091e402cd3754aa40eaf56cb16cc2f87668a9c915e8a2.webp)

3. Remove the fastener between the right front lower swing arm assembly and the ball stud press assembly.

a. Remove 2 fixing nut. Tightening torque: 90N m
b. Remove fixing bolt. Tightening torque: 90N m

4. Remove the right front lower swing arm assembly.

a. Remove 1 fixing nut, and take out 1 fixing bolt. Tightening torque: 200N m
b. Remove 1 fixing nut, take out 1 fixing bolt, and take out the right front lower swing arm assembly. Tightening torque: 200N m

### ? Caution:

Take out the right front lower swing arm assembly with the assistance of another maintenance technician.

1. Install in the reverse order of removal.

2. Wheel alignment must be carried out after installation. See Wheel Alignment

### Removal and Installation of Ball Stud Press Assembly

? Reminder:

The removal and installation of the left and right ball stud press assembly are the same. The following is an example of the left front ball pin press-fit assembly.

### Removal

1. Remove the left front wheel assembly. See Installation and Removal of Wheel Assembly

![](images/cd462098c88f78c55f4b61f31a133ba96fdfebaaaf1b33ebe7e5a11236da947a.webp)

![](images/ba7c1e75e3462e4a8bc6166add231560acf2bcb4bdb58863852afad09add6fed.webp)

2. Detach the left front lower swing arm assembly.

a. Remove 2 fixing nuts of the left front lower swing arm assembly. Tightening torque: 90N m
b. Remove 1 fixing bolt of the left front lower swing arm assembly. Tightening torque: 90N m
c. Detach the left front lower swing arm assembly downwards.

3. Remove the fasteners of the ball stud press assembly and lower swing arm. a. Remove 1 fixing pin. b. Remove 1 fixing nut. Tightening torque: 100N m

4. Remove the ball stud assembly with a ball joint remover.

Installation

### A Caution:

Check whether the shock absorber strut assembly leaks oil after removing, and replace it with a new one if it leaks oil.

### Overview

The front suspension system of this model adopts McPherson independent suspension, which occupies small space, has light weight, good comfort and is easy to handle.

The main function of the shock absorber is to buffer the impact force transmitted to the frame or body from uneven road, reduce the vibration caused thereby, ensure the smooth running and improve the comfort of the driver and passengers.

### Removal

1. Remove the left front wheel assembly. See Installation and Removal of Wheel Assembly

2. Remove the ventilation cover assembly. See Installation and Removal of the Ventilation Cover Assembly

3. Remove the front wiper drive system assembly. See Installation and Removal of Front Wiper Drive System Assembly

![](images/97a976ee93e66b471b611ce145abbe6c73854ebd2016bb492a72f6055004e172.webp)

4. Detach the front compartment harness from the left front shock absorber strut assembly.

![](images/50dd268e79224d8dd3e70b14306985281b264ecd18d23ab11c8c64b29b462b1e.webp)

5. Detach the left front brake hose assembly from the left front shock absorber strut assembly.

a. Remove 1 fixing bolt. Tightening torque: 30N m b. Detach the left front brake hose assembly.

![](images/3e2b662c67f4432bffc8504eb789552ab95bd6927cad2d3697e5b3d27180b578.webp)

6. Remove 4 fixing nut, and detach the left front stabilizer bar tie rod and ball joint assembly and left front shock absorber strut assembly.

Tightening torque: 90N m

A Caution:

When removing the front stabilizer bar tie rod and ball joint assembly, fix the intermediate stud and then remove the fixing nut.

![](images/ee2ce1a046a260c89f01720b1d234e5c952e576d6db48774ec92c34e85c92394.webp)

![](images/78fca20cd706ff2dd4efe7ddf001ee6cd0af701610dd9c8468fdf468cec95470.webp)

Installation

7. Remove 2 fixing nuts, take out 2 fixing bolts, and detach the left front steering knuckle from the left front shock absorber strut assembly.

Tightening torque: 200N m

8. Remove 3 fixing bolts, and take out the left front shock absorber strut assembly.

Tightening torque: 55N m

? Caution:

Take out the left front shock absorber strut assembly with the assistance of another maintenance technician.

1. Install in the reverse order of removal. 2. Four wheel alignment must be carried out after installation. See Wheel Alignment

### Removal

1. Remove the right front wheel assembly. See Installation and Removal of Wheel Assembly

2. Remove the ventilation cover assembly. See Installation and Removal of the Ventilation Cover Assembly

3. Remove the front wiper drive system assembly. Installation and Removal of Front Wiper Drive System Assembly

![](images/a28e748db1fa85a4b5bb3bd6dd6e5589db31c2ed2eeb421ae68ed8f585fb65be.webp)

4. Detach the front compartment harness from the right front shock absorber strut assembly.

![](images/7055a7b732f3df61ee9f08f78db603c5eb1249b1c81d1a175175ce727d661a12.webp)

5. Detach the right front brake hose assembly from the right front shock absorber strut assembly.

a. Remove the 1 fixing bolts. Tightening torque: 30N m b. Detach the right front brake hose assembly.

![](images/ee6f5116c8bf7206eead6fbf625ed3625ba9421b6ce3c610b350b6ef9f4bf64b.webp)

6. Remove 1 fixing nut, and detach the right front stabilizer bar tie rod and ball joint assembly from right front shock absorber strut assembly.

Tightening torque: 90N m

A Caution:

Please secure bolt with a suitable tool and then remove the fixing nut when removing the front stabilizer bar tie rod and ball joint assembly.

![](images/c7860b7e114f07c0455b7a3c48d3d55a7b4aaa47cf6045812820421b9f82646e.webp)

![](images/07e06142b3ce95168a8d6b0ed48afa67acf115aadd22f7ec6ca5497b36c28d5a.webp)

Installation

7. Remove 2 fixing nuts, take out 2 fixing bolts, and detach the right front steering knuckle from the right front shock absorber strut assembly.

Tightening torque: 200N m

8. Remove 3 fixing bolts, and take out the right front shock absorber strut assembly.

Tightening torque: 55N m

? Caution:

Take out the right front shock absorber strut assembly with the assistance of another maintenance technician.

1. Install in the reverse order of removal. 2. Four wheel alignment must be carried out after installation. See Wheel Alignment

### A Caution:

To replace the front stabilizer bar fitting
assembly, the front subframe assembly must be dropped from the body and then the front stabilizer bar fitting assembly must be removed.
Before installing the front stabilizer bar
fitting assembly, check whether the rubber sleeve is damaged, otherwise replace the front stabilizer bar fitting assembly with a new one.
Please secure bolt with a suitable tool and then remove the fixing nut when removing the front stabilizer bar tie rod and ball joint assembly.

### Overview

The function of the stabilizer bar is to prevent the excessive lateral roll of the body during cornering and to keep the body balanced. The purpose is to reduce the degree of lateral roll and improve smoothness.

### nstallation and Removal of Tie Rod and Ball Assembly of Front Transverse Stabilizer Bar

? Reminder:

The removal and installation of the left and right front stabilizer bar tie rod and ball joint assemblies are the same. Take the left front stabilizer bar tie rod and ball joint assembly as the example.

### Removal

1. Remove the left front wheel assembly. See Installation and Removal of Wheel Assembly

![](images/bdc8cad9763a2c1cd426fa04392c752f0433423511ebbc455e46078221db58dd.webp)

2. Remove 2 fixing bolts, and take out the front stabilizer bar link and ball joint assembly.

Tightening torque: 90N m

A Caution:

Installation

1. Install in the reverse order of removal.

### Removal

1. Remove the front subframe and powertrain. See Installation and Removal of Front Subframe and Powertrain

![](images/91d61a87b00ca8e6766e776a1d0545a1cc38611ad497ac3fe2f769a6352b0187.webp)

Installation

2. Remove 4 fixing bolts and take out front stabilizer bar fitting assembly. Tightening torque: 60N m

1. Install in the reverse order of removal.

### A Caution:

To replace the rear torsion beam assembly, remove fixing bolts of the rear torsion beam bracket from the vehicle body, remove the torsion beam assembly together with the bracket, and then disassemble them. Do not disassemble the shock absorber strut assembly for maintenance. After removal, check the shock absorber strut assembly for oil leakage. In case of oil leakage, replace the assembly with a new one.

### Overview

The rear suspension system of this model uses a torsion beam type non-independent suspension, which is space-efficient, light and comfortable, and is easy to control.

The torsion beam type non-independent suspension balances the up and down bounce of left and right wheels through a torsion beam to reduce vehicle shaking and keep the vehicle stable.

The shock absorber is mainly used to buffer the impact force transmitted from uneven road surface to the frame or the vehicle body, reduce the vibration caused by it, ensure the smooth running, and improve the comfort of the driver and passengers.

### Removal

1. Remove the left rear wheel assembly. See Installation and Removal of Wheel Assembly
2. Remove the right rear wheel assembly. See Installation and Removal of Wheel Assembly
3. Remove the left rear brake disc. See Removal and installation of rear brake disc
4. Remove the right rear brake disc. See Removal and installation of rear brake disc
5. Remove the rear wheel hub unit assembly. See Installation and Removal of Rear Wheel Hub Unit Assembly
6. Remove the upper cushion of rear coil spring. See Installation and Removal of Upper Cushion of Rear Coil Spring
7. Remove the lower cushion of rear coil spring. See Installation and Removal of Lower Cushion of Rear Coil Spring

![](images/01ca31b36e9d3b9f5df6d9babf3f458b694986a99948e23f28876521d45ef038.webp)

8. Remove 2 fixing nut of rear shock absorber assembly and take out 2 fixing bolt.

Tightening torque: 120N m

### A Caution:

Before taking out the fixing bolts of the rear shock absorber assembly, use equipment to support the rear torsion beam assembly.

9. Remove 8 fixing bolts from the left and right mounting bracket assembly of the rear torsion beam.

Tightening torque: 120N m

![](images/aa6c7a17ab3e971e1f11640c3be0ecafb4490497d4497754764a687fe12d58c8.webp)

10. Remove 1 fixing nut, take out 4 fixing bolt 1 and the left mounting bracket assembly of the rear torsion beam.

Tightening torque: 160N m

Installation

### A Caution:

When installing the fasteners of the rear torsion beam mounting bracket assembly, tighten them by hand, install the rear torsion beam assembly on the vehicle body, use the equipment to support it to a proper position, and then tighten them to the standard torque.

1. Install in the reverse order of removal.

### Removal and Installation of Rear Coil Spring

![](images/4424b4944c2f05996f8bc6d6762098f0013ee53b7d676b4b307f6ed14c185340.webp)

The removal and installation of the left and right rear coil springs are the same. Take the left as an example.

### Removal

1. Remove the left rear wheel. See Installation and Removal of Wheel Assembly

![](images/6a118b0f3cd8d41123d4acb651b045a0276a9e747b27f90325ac2180f80385d8.webp)

2. Clamp out the rear coil spring with the device.

### A Caution:

When compressing the rear coil spring, it must be fixed firmly to avoid personal injury.

Installation

### A Caution:

Before installing the rear coil spring, check whether the upper and lower cushions of the rear coil spring are damaged. If so, replace them with new ones.
When installed, the upper and lower cushion notches of the rear coil spring must be matched with the end of the rear coil spring.

1. Install in the reverse order of removal.

The removal and installation of the left and right rear coil spring upper cushions are the same. Take the left as an example.

When installed, the upper cushion notches of the rear coil spring must be matched with the end of the rear coil spring.

Installation

### ? Caution:

When installing the lower cushion of the rear coil spring, the raised point must be installed into the opening of the torsion beam tray.
When installed, the lower cushion notches of the rear coil spring must be matched with the end of the rear coil spring.

1. Install in the reverse order of removal.

### A Caution:

Lift the vehicle according to the standard operation process.
When performing operations under a lifted vehicle, install safety devices, and wear a safety helmet and appropriate PPE to prevent accidental injury.
Do not knock parts with hard objects such as a metal hammer during maintenance to prevent damage to parts.
Please clean the outer surfaces of parts before disassembly and assembly.
Tighten the fixing bolts to the standard
torque after each component of suspension system is installed.
Perform a road test on the vehicle on the premise of ensuring safety and complying with local traffic laws and regulations.
Do not attempt driving operations that may endanger the vehicle.

### Overview

The suspension is mainly used to alleviate the impact from uneven road on wheels, determine the positions of wheels and axles, and improve the grip performance of wheels on road. Therefore, the suspension has a certain impact on the riding comfort and handling stability of the vehicle. The rear suspension of the vehicle is a multi-link independent suspension. It has the advantage that the left and right wheels can bounce separately. The wheels do not interfere with each other, which can reduce the inclination and vibration of the vehicle body, reduce the impact on the vehicle body, and improve the comfort of the rear seat.

### ? Warning:

Cracked tires can be dangerous. Before removing a cracked tire, exhaust the air from the vehicle. Failure to follow this operation may cause serious personal injury. When install the wheel and tire, the model must be matched. Does not match the installation may cause the tire bead to break or the tire to detach from the wheel.

### ? Caution:

When remove the counterweight, do not use sharp metal tools such as screwdrivers to prevent wheel damage. Counterweight remover must be used for removal. Do not use wire brush or strong detergent to clean the wheel, otherwise, the wheel will be damaged. The standard tire pressure has an important effect on the life of the tire. The tire pressure must be charged to the standard value after installation.

### Systems Manual

Overview

The wheel assembly is composed of aluminum alloy wheel and tire.

Correct tire pressure, wheel alignment and driving skills have a significant impact on tire life.

Driving habits such as sharp cornering, rapidly accelerating and hard braking can accelerate the wear of the tires.

Structure of Tire

![](images/6e66bc324610cde6ba5cf5a6a42fc7a60509a679e2c62ce3ed473bea68bbd229.webp)

1. Belted layer

The steel cord between the tread and the carcass protects the carcass, suppresses the deformation of the tread, maintains the ground of the tread, and improves the wear resistance and driving stability.

2. Crown layer

The special cord ply above the belt layer can restrain the movement of the belt ply during tire driving, prevent the belt ply from separating at high speed, and keep the tire dimensional stability at high speed.

3. Tread

The part of the tire in contact with the road surface must have the driving and braking performance through friction, and must have good wear resistance, puncture resistance, impact resistance, heat dissipation and other performance.

4. Tire

The cord ply in the tire is the main stressed component in the tire, which is impact

resistant with good flex resistance during driving.

5. Bead

The tape-hanging wire is wound according to a certain shape (quadrilateral or hexagonal shape) to install the tire onto the rim fixing tire.

6. Air impervious liner

The airtight part of the inner tube-free tire is made of special rubber, which is equivalent to the function of the inner tube.

7. Bead filler strip

The padding on the bead in the tire prevents bead dispersion, slows bead impact, protects the bead and prevents air from entering during molding.

Meaning of Sidewall Mark of Tire and Description of Air Pressure

![](images/0058d224cc9edb05bfedf6d55284fd22255b95fb8919339daeed2359d07917e8.webp)
Meaning of sidewall marking of tire

![](images/5862b98d6e3560452b8a6009c2e5b33a0511dc521055f2ded1926f61e1a02e82.webp)

![](images/2dfe959fcb3502e47524b60b59112cccf32874a47faa2c76948d8b7700d94cbc.webp)

Corresponding table of common speed classes

Standard tire pressure
![](images/1b4abcbf61aa574b3b689fe46f495532765e2540fc10f6a4093365ecce04c760.webp)

![](images/30ab8559435f0bdbd103cf9f9a0e6f23e402625752e84555dbe853b8ab3fc345.webp)

Meaning of tire pressure and description of air pressure

Tire pressure has a decisive influence on the wear and tear of the tire, so it is necessary to maintain the standard pressure and check the pressure regularly for safe driving.

The load capacity of the tire corresponds to its inflation pressure, and the reasonable air pressure of the tire must be determined according to the load of the vehicle. Changes in climate and seasons must not be a reason to adjust tire pressure.

In the early stage of the new tire, the outer rim size of the tire will change due to the heat of flexion movement, which will reduce the tire pressure. Therefore, the air pressure must be checked and adjusted after 24 hours of use or driving 2000-3000 km.

### Systems Manual

The tire pressure must be increased by 10%-15% for driving with a high speed for a long time.

Hazards of insufficient air pressure:

Insufficient air pressure will cause tire sidewall deformation and increase heat generation, greatly reducing tire life and leading to the following problems and safety hazards:

Excessive wear at the shoulder.
Increase the possible bulging caused by tire impact.
A loss of adhesion between the various parts of the tire causes the delamination.
A loss of adhesion between the various parts of the tire causes the delamination.
Seriously insufficient air pressure causes sidewall rolling damage.
Excessive tire runout causes abnormal
abrasion between bead and rim with damage for rim.
The rolling resistance increases and the
power consumption increases.

Hazards of excessive air pressure:

Excessive air pressure will reduce the ground area of the tire tread, increase the rigidity of the carcass, and reduce the cushioning performance, and the following problems and potentia safety hazards will be caused:

Excessive wear at the center of the tread. Increase the risk of tire rupture or even blowout when impacted by external forces. The decrease of grounding area will result in the decrease of controllability and easy to cause drift, sliding and other hazards. Passenger comfort is reduced. Poor ride comfort and long-term running with excessive air pressure may cause damage to the vehicle chassis.

Uneven tire pressure on the same suspension can lead to:

The braking force is not evenly left and right. Steering wheel deflection. Reduced maneuverability. Deflection during acceleration. The vehicle deviates during driving. Component Position Diagram

### Wheel Changing

Due to the different loads on the front and rear tires of the vehicle during operation, the wear will also be very different. Therefore, in order to avoid the wear of the tires in a single direction, regular and timely transposition can make the tire wear evenly, thus prolonging the life of the tire. Conduct tire rotation every 5000-8000 km, and the main purpose is:

Ensure uniform wear and fatigue of tire, and ensure stability and economy.
Check the condition of the tire during transposition, find out the damage in time to prevent accidents.
When changing the tires, ensure that the steering tire is the best tire to improve the stability and safety of the vehicle.

Tire rotation method:

1. Remove 4 wheel assemblies from the vehicle.
2. Install the wheel 1# to the original installation position of wheel 4#.
3. Install the wheel 4# to the original installation position of wheel 2#.
4. Install the wheel 2# to the original installation position of wheel 3#.
5. Install the wheel 3# to the original installation position of wheel 1#.

![](images/d7c7694b3c9cb0afec9c34abae1eeaa10a825b250ae64efbd0889c3bcf581e96.webp)

### Wheel alignment parameter value

![](images/073ccb97acaa3280debd7eb3a64e69ca501d75b496753d1bb70c7f64fd27c056.webp)

Toe-in angle of front wheel

### A Caution:

In this model, only the toe-in value of the front wheel can be adjusted through the steering rod, and other parameters of wheel alignment cannot be adjusted.

1. Inspection before four-wheel alignment:

a. Release the parking brake to avoid incorrect measurement.
b. Make sure that the suspension device is not changed.
c. Make sure that the 4 tires are of the same specification, and that the tire pressure is within the specified range.
d. Make sure that there are no people or extra loads in the vehicle.
e. Check whether each fixing point of suspension is loose and deformed, and check the clearance of suspension ball heads to ensure it is not too large.
f. Check the wheels for vibration.
g. Check to confirm that both sides of the vehicle are level with each other.
h. The steering wheel alignment tolerance is 0° ±0.2
i. Carry out a dynamic balance test on wheels, and install them back on the vehicle after the test.
j. Make the wheels bounce up and down several times to stabilize the suspension.
k. The test bench is in normal condition.
l. Adjust the rear wheels first and then the front wheels.

2. Test:

a. Check the wheel alignment according to the operating instructions of the fourwheel aligner.

![](images/8615db77b70efbbb55842d34212c77e6f5ecf100573abcbf2e799c364ecaba62.webp)

3. Adjust the front wheel toe-in. a. Loosen the steering link lock nut. b. Place 1 open-end wrench at the hexagonal position of the steering links, and adjust the front wheel toe-in to the standard value by rotating the left or right link. Front wheel toe-in value: 1.3±1.82mm c. Tighten the lock nut. Tightening torque: 70 N•m

### Reminder:

The adjustment methods of the rear left and rear right wheel total toe-ins are the same.

![](images/bc19eb28f1ceb6d32d5f85d215f9cd70abdc45d965b3fa6f2d580619f1a76d43.webp)

4. Adjustment of rear wheel toe-in

? Reminder:

The adjustment methods of the rear left and rear right wheel total toe-ins are the same.

a. Fix the eccentric bolt with a tool.
b. Loosen the lock nut.
c. Rotate the rear wheel toe-in adjusting eccentric bolt until the toe-in is correct. Rear wheel toe-in value: 1.56±3.56mm
d. After adjustment, fix the eccentric bolt and tighten the lock nut. Tightening torque: 70 N•m

### A Caution:

The connection points of camber
eccentric bolts can only be installed and removed once after sales. After this, nuts need to be replaced with new ones. Bolts and gaskets should be replaced as needed. In case of rust, it is
recommended to replace them with new ones.
Make sure that the gasket and eccentric bolt gasket are both properly seated in the limit groove.

![](images/b6710eaba81d89db31bfa811f1d6b14054aeaa82ee115df27f48fc5bb8becd4c.webp)

5. Adjustment of rear wheel camber angle.

? Reminder:

The adjustment methods of the rear left and rear right wheel camber angles are the same.

a. Fix the eccentric bolt with a tool.
b. Loosen the lock nut.
c. Rotate the eccentric bolt for adjusting the rear wheel camber angle until the camber angle is correct. Rear wheel camber angle: -1.07±0.5

d. After adjustment, fix the eccentric bolt and tighten the lock nut. Tightening torque: 70 N•m

Avoid oil contact with skin. If it is accidentally splashed into the eyes, immediately rinse with plenty of water and seek medical attention as soon as possible.

After connecting the intelligent power braking system push rod and the brake pedal, do not pull the pedal upward, otherwise the internal structural parts of the intelligent power braking system may be damaged.

The stop light switch clearance needs to be adjusted after replacing the intelligent power braking system.

One hand must hold the electric machine and the other hand as an auxiliary to move it when moving the intelligent power braking system. Never grab ECU ports, push rods, brake fluid reservoirs, motors and mounting plate with one hand.

Plug the removed brake tube and the interface of intelligent power braking system to avoid foreign bodies entering.

Do not bend the pipe during the removal of the hard tube. Otherwise, the brake fluid flow will be reduced and the braking effect will be reduced.

### System descriptions Overview

The IPB system includes a brake booster and a brake adjustment module, which replaces the traditional EVP+ESC module, greatly reducing the weight of the whole system. The decoupled brake system is used to solve the problem of vehicle brake feedback.

The IPB system consists of the following functions:

The anti-lock brake system (ABS) can control the brakeforce in a real-time manner during emergency braking to prevent deviation and sideslip, so that the vehicle can always maintain good directional stability and operability, and the safety of vehicle braking can be improved.

The electronic brakeforce distribution (EBD) system is used to balance the effective grip force of each wheel before ABS action in case that the wheels are locked during emergency braking. This can prevent drifting and side shifting and shorten the braking distance.

The traction control system (TCS) enables the vehicle to obtain the best traction under various driving conditions. The system receives the driver's steering intention through the steering wheel angle sensor, and then detects the speed difference between the left and right wheels with the left and right wheel speed sensors, so as to judge whether the vehicle steering conforms to the driver's steering intention. If understeer (or oversteer) is detected, the system immediately judges that the drive force of the drive wheel is too large, and issues an instruction to reduce the drive force, so as to realize the driver's steering intention.

The hill-start hold control (HHC) system is derived from the ESP system. It allows the vehicle to keep braking for seconds when the driver's right foot leaves the brake pedal if the vehicle starts on a hill when the handbrake is not applicable, so that the driver can easily move his/her foot from the brake pedal to the accelerator pedal, and accidents due to sliding can be avoided. Therefore, the system makes the driver operate more easily.

The hydraulic brake assist (HBA) system can help the driver to apply emergency braking. It judges whether there is a need for full

braking based on the speed at which the driver depresses the brake pedal. As long as the driver keeps depressing the pedal to the floor, the system will automatically increase the brakeforce until the threshold of ABS starting is reached. If the driver releases the brake pedal, the system will reduce the brakeforce to the specified value.

Controller deceleration parking (CDP): Nowadays, the vehicle is generally equipped with the EPB instead of traditional handbrake, and there is an EPB switch on the vehicle. The CDP can enable the EPB switch to act as a traditional handbrake (the EPB switch can be pulled to brake the vehicle dynamically when the vehicle is running).

The vehicle dynamic control (VDC) system is used to improve the driving stability, but it cannot prevent accidents caused by rapid sharp turns or careless or dangerous driving operations.

The automatic vehicle hold (AVH) system has the function of automatically pulling the handbrake. After this function is activated, for example, when the vehicle stops at traffic lights, the driver does not need to pull the handbrake. This function is especially suitable for going up and down hills and frequently starting and stopping the vehicle.

### System descriptions Overview

The electronic stability system (ESS) is a braking system that prevents the vehicle from slipping under emergency driving conditions. Activeness is one of its main characteristics. Unlike the ABS which reacts passively, it can nip trouble in the bud.

### Reminder:

The method for draining the brake fluid of the front and rear wheels is the same. Take the left rear side as an example.

![](images/dcc30fbfe202aad327400609fe6f57f71a5998b453c78b7f4dad6281ad022683.webp)

1. Remove the bleed bolt cover.

![](images/de7ce784d9dbf7859df1676fcffc0bcf4e7617dd5e34f9461c230fd8dbb630da.webp)

2. Connect the brake fluid collection container with the bleed screw, and loosen the bleed screw.

3. Press the brake pedal and gradually drain all brake fluid.

Filling

### A Caution:

Check whether there is dirt in the brake fluid reservoir before filling. Do not refill used brake fluid, and fill brake fluid of the same specification as requi

### A Caution:

Ensure that the brake fluid level is within the specified range after filling.

1. Open the filler cap of brake fluid reservoir and add brake fluid.

![](images/ec603588b83b52607d80e40b1324b54c70870d8fca0f228d74a3f2b52ab65028.webp)

2. Loosen the bleed screw, slowly press the brake pedal to the bottom, and then release it. Repeat this operation every 2-3s until new brake fluid is discharged from the bleed screw.

3. Then press the brake pedal and tighten the bleed screw.
4. Carry out same operations for other 3 wheels.
5. Detect the water content of brake fluid with a brake fluid detector. If the measured result shows that there is no water in the brake fluid, this round of brake fluid replacement is completed.
6. Bleed the brake system. Refer to Air Discharge of Brake System
7. Install the

bleed bolt cover.

### A Caution:

– Do not reuse any brake fluid discharged. The brake fluid is corrosive to paint. Remove any brake fluid accidentally splashing on the body paint with a cloth as soon as possible.
– Please take caution to avoid skin contact with brake fluid. In the event of accidental splashing into any eye, rinse immediately with plenty of water and seek medical attention as soon as
possible. Please refrain from discharging brake fluid arbitrarily and ensure that it is recycled in accordance with local regulations. Be sure to use genuine Sinopec HZY6 brake fluid. Using nonspecified brake fluid may cause corrosion and shorten the service life of the brake system. Bleeding requires brake fluid pressurizing equipment and VDS. Before bleeding, ensure that the brake fluid of pressurizing equipment is sufficient (about 2L), and set the filling pressure to
2 bar (0.2 MPa). Check that the filler cap is properly tightened; otherwise, the brake fluid will spray out.
– After bleeding, make up the brake fluid or remove excess brake fluid as required to ensure that the fluid level is between the MIN and MAX marks of the brake fluid reservoir.

Brake system bleeding methods

Wet-type bleeding

Circumstances requiring wet-type bleeding: after replacing or removing and installing brake calipers, brake hoses, and brake pipes.

Dry-type bleeding

Circumstances requiring dry-type bleeding: after replacing the brake fluid, replacing the IPB system, removing and replacing brake calipers, brake hoses, and brake pipes directly without entering the "installation mode" of the IPB system first, or after failure in wet bleeding.

Wet-type bleeding

### A Caution:

– Use VDS to set the intelligent power braking system to "installation mode" and then change parts; if this operation isn preformed before replacement or removal and installation of the brake caliper, brake hose and brake pipe, dry air discharge must be carried out.
After air discharge, the ABS, ESC or braking system alarm must not be issued by the instrument panel of the vehicle, and the brake pedal must be depressed normally without producing any abnormal sounds.
The filling pressure (2 bar) of the brake fluid reservoir must not be increased, otherwise the brake fluid pot may be damaged.

1. Power on the vehicle.

![](images/42fa2a7cd0f3133513e1151eb37c053b8be17d83ebb86acc37a9406f4ac30857.webp)

2. Set the IPB system to "installation mode" with the VDS.

b. Select the corresponding vehicle series.
c. Select the corresponding vehicle model.
d. Scan.
e. Select the "Electro-hydraulic brake (Bosch)" module.
f. Select "Calibration".
g. Select "Installation mode" for calibration.

3. Power off the vehicle.

4. Connect the brake fluid pressurizing equipment, and make sure that the pressurizing equipment and the brake fluid reservoir opening are well sealed and firmly fixed without leakage.
5. Connect the brake fluid collection container with the bleed screw via a clean and transparent exhaust hose.
6. Turn on the brake fluid pressurizing equipment to increase the pressure to 2 bar, then loosen the brake bleed screw, and press the brake pedal normally once every 2 s until the brake fluid from the bleed hose is free of air bubbles, indicating that the air has been completely discharged. Press the brake pedal, and tighten the bleed screw.

A Caution:

Air discharge is only required for the removed hydraulic circuit.

Check and confirm that the ABS, ESC or braking system alarm is not issued by the instrument panel of the vehicle and the brake pedal is depressed normally without producing abnormal sounds (which indicates that the air discharge is successful).

a. Connect the VDS and tap "Vehicle diagnosis system" to select "Passenger car".
