### Entry and Immobilizer System Central door lock system

System descriptions

Overview

Central control: The driver can lock or unlock all doors at the same time by pressing the smart key or the lock/unlock button on the front left window regulator panel.

Speed control: When the vehicle reaches a certain speed, all doors are automatically locked by sensing to prevent passengers from accidentally opening doors while the vehicle is running.

![](images/4835db46ae2408cb15be15d4c10544a665d51089d38d571c55b5d6252fae2e39.webp)

2. Remove the vehicle lock cylinder and key assembly.

Installation

1. Install it in the reverse order of removal.

### A Caution:

Do not put the smart key in the high
temperature area.
Do not use a hard object to hit or throw the smart key.
Keep the smart key away from the
magnetic field.
If you do not use the vehicle after the
door is locked and it has entered the antitheft state, keep the smart key away from the vehicle, because the communication of the vehicle's automatic card search will consume the power of the low-voltage battery.
The smart key may fail when the power of the key is low.
The smart key may fail if the strong
magnetic field or electric field, such as the TV signal tower and the like, is around the detection system.
The smart key may fail if it is shielded by a metal item.
The smart key may fail if it is put together with the cellphone.
The smart key may fail if the electronic
smart key system of a nearby vehicle is running.

### Overview

For this model, in addition to the traditional mechanical key, the electronic smart key system is configured for this vehicle, thus enabling the driver who carries this key to open the door without any operation of the key via buttons.

The system is controlled by an smart key system control module in the left body control module. When the smart key system control module detects that the key is within a certain detection area, it will verify the key and send a running signal to the ECU that will perform corresponding actions.

The detection system is composed of 5 detection antenna assemblies and used for detecting the valid range in the vehicle and the certain range outside the vehicle.

### ? Warning:

Do not touch the iron battery negative
harness to the iron battery positive pole. It is forbidden to discharge to the fire.
It is forbidden to disassemble, modify or use external charger to charge the iron battery without permission.
When the power is low and the vehicle
enters sleep protection, it is required to wake up the vehicle by pressing the
microswitch on the left front door handle or the front compartment, and power on the vehicle to start DC power up for about 15 minutes.
Inflammable and explosive materials are prohibited from approaching iron batteries.
Keep children away from iron batteries.

### Systems Manual Overview

The start iron battery is the source of the lowvoltage power of the electronic equipment of the vehicle. In order to guarantee the normal operation of the low voltage system, the design of the vehicle must try to ensure that the iron battery will not lose power, so it increases the intelligent charging system in the traditional design. When the vehicle is parked for a long time, there is no need to disconnect the negative electrode of the iron battery. When the battery detector detects that the iron battery is too low, it can charge the iron battery with the power battery to ensure that the iron battery will not lose power.

### Instrument and Warning System Instrument panel cluster

System descriptions

Overview

The instrument panel cluster is located right in front of the driver and at the upper part of the steering column, providing the driver with required vehicle operation parameters, faults, mileage and other information.

The lighting of the instrument panel cluster is realized through adjustable LEDs located behind it, so as to illuminate the meters to achieve the necessary visibility. Each indicator on the instrument panel cluster is also illuminated through special LEDs. Each LED is integrally welded to the circuit board behind the instrument panel cluster housing. The connecting circuits connect the instrument panel cluster to the electrical system of the vehicle. They are integrated in the vehicle wiring harness, routed to different positions and fixed in many different ways.

### A Caution:

Dropping of any tire pressure monitoring module should be avoided during its removal and installation.

It is necessary to re-match and learn the new tire pressure monitoring module after replacement.

It is necessary to re-match and learn the tire pressure monitoring module after tire rotation.

The removed tire pressure monitoring module should be kept in a dry and clean place.

Installing additional accessories on the vehicle may interfere with the normal operation of the tire pressure monitoring system.

Driving near a high voltage power wire or a wireless transmitter may interfere with the normal operation of the tire pressure monitoring system.

### System descriptions Overview

The TPMS directly measures parameters such as tire pressure and acceleration with the pressure sensor in each tire and sends the collected data through wireless RF to the receiving module which demodulates, analyzes and processes the RF data as CAN signals. Finally, the tire-related information is displayed digitally through instrument panel cluster in a real time manner. When the pressure of any tire exceeds the set normal threshold, the system will send alarms to driver in audible and visual form to ensure driving safety.

### Driver Assistance Cruise control system

System descriptions

Overview

The cruise control system allows driving at a preset speed above 40 km/h without pressing the accelerator pedal. This function may be activated for driving on a straight, uncrowded expressway.

Based on conventional cruise control, the adaptive cruise control (ACC) system is designed to actively control the vehicle speed for auto follow-up while cruising. This is done via a camera which detects the vehicle's distance and speed relative to the vehicle ahead. The ACC system can automatically switch between fixed-speed cruise and followup cruise depending on whether there is a vehicle ahead.

The cruise control button is used to set the cruise speed and the headway between the vehicle and a vehicle ahead. Vehicle speed can be set from 30 to 150 km/h, or the headway between the vehicle and a vehicle ahead can be set, so the vehicle can follow the vehicle ahead at a cruise speed of 0 to 150 km/h.

### A Caution:

When dirt or snow is attached to the sensor, the sensor freezes or the sensor is covered by hands, sensor may not work properly.

When the vehicle is exposed to the sun or extremely low temperature, the detection range of the sensor may change.

When the vehicle is running on a rough road, the vehicle has a large inclination angle, the vehicle is driving toward a higher curb, or another vehicle equipped with a sensor is approaching, the sensor may have false detection.

The sensor may not be able to detect objects that absorb sound waves, such as cotton, snows, objects with sharp edges, objects that are too low, too high or protruding top of objects, or when the sensor is subjected to a strong impact or collision, or linear objects.

### System descriptions Overview

The parking assist system is a vehicular monitoring system developed by applying the detection principle used by bats in flight. Several ultrasonic radar probes are installed at the front and rear of a vehicle to transmit and receive signals and provide feedback information to a controller. The controller

calculates the distance from the vehicle to an obstacle based on the turn-back time and triggers different sounds and indicator alarms based on the distance to alert a driver of the distance between the obstacle and the vehicle. This increases the reversing and parking convenience and safety.

### System descriptions Overview

The panoramic view system includes two main functions: 2D panoramic view and transparent panoramic view. In R gear, these functions will be triggered automatically. Users can also activate and enable these functions manually by pressing the hard button on the steering wheel or the APP soft button on the touchscreen homepage. The image is input through four 720P high-definition cameras and transmitted through the LVDS interface at a rate of 30 frames per second.

It is mainly used to provide the user with a reversing image during reversing, to help the user complete parking faster. The user can use this function by turning on APP button on the touchscreen homepage if necessary or by shifting into R gear.

### A Caution:

ACC is a system to enhance comfort, rather than a safety system, nor an obstacle detector or collision warning system. The driver must maintain control of the vehicle at all times, and is fully responsible for the vehicle's operation.

The ACC function can assist the driver, but it cannot replace the driver in driving. The driver must always maintain control of the vehicle and be fully responsible for the vehicle, following traffic regulations at all times.

For safety, ACC cannot be activated when ESC is not turned on.

ACC is suitable for use on expressways and roads in good conditions, but unsuitable for use on complex urban roads or mountain roads.

Maintaining a proper distance from a vehicle ahead is the responsibility of the driver. The following distance of the ACC system shall meet the minimum distance requirements as stipulated by various countries for the specific driving environment.

When the ACC is active, if the driver presses the accelerator pedal or brake pedal, the control of the vehicle will be handed over to the driver, and the ACC system will no longer keep a safe distance from the vehicle ahead.

If a vehicle ahead brakes suddenly (emergency stop), ACC may fail to react or be slow in reacting to the vehicle ahead, resulting in the risk of late braking. In this case, the driver does not receive a takeover request.

In some cases (a vehicle ahead running slowly, the vehicle changing lanes too suddenly, or keeping excessively short safety distance), ACC may not have enough time to reduce the relative speed. In such cases, the driver must react appropriately. ACC cannot provide an audio or visual alarm in each case.

### ? Caution:

When ACC is activated while the vehicle is stationary, it may identify any stationary obstacle in front as a vehicle, so it may then keep the vehicle stationary to ensure a safe starting and avoid collision with the stationary target caused by unexpected starting. However, this function cannot identify all obstacles, so the driver must ensure that there are no obstacles or other traffic participants in front of the vehicle.

If the vehicle with ACC activated runs too close to an adjacent lane (or another vehicle on an adjacent lane runs too close to the lane on which the vehicle with ACC activated is running), ACC may apply braking in response to the corresponding vehicle.

If another vehicle changes to the lane on which the vehicle with ACC activated is running and falls within the detection range of the front mmWave radar, it may be identified as a target vehicle, and a response may be made correspondingly. In this event, forced braking or late braking may occur.

In some circumstances, detection may be affected or delayed. If the front mmWave radar reflection cross-sectional area of the target is too small (e.g., a bicycle, carriage, or pedestrian), there is a risk that ACC may be unable to identify the distance from the target ahead, resulting in late response or no response to these targets. In such cases, the driver needs to control the vehicle speed. Moreover, the detection may be affected by noise or electromagnetic interference, resulting in delay or interference.

When the overlap between the vehicle and the vehicle ahead is too small, the ACC system may be unable to identify the vehicle ahead as the target. In this event, the driver needs to keep control of the vehicle.

When the vehicle follows a vehicle ahead to stop, ACC is unable to identify the end of the target vehicle ahead and instead identifies its lower end (e.g. the rear axle of a truck with high chassis or the bumper of a vehicle) in very few cases. Should these

A Caution: occur, ACC is unable to ensure a proper stopping distance, and the driver must stay vigilant and ready to brake at any time. Structural retrofitting of the vehicle, such as lowering the chassis or changing the front license plate frame, may compromise the ACC system. Do not use the ACC system when driving on roads with poor visibility, ramps, or multiple curves, or on slippery and wet roads with snow, ice, or water gathered. In the following situations, professional calibration and checking of the front mmWave radar and multi-purpose camera must be performed by a BYD authorized dealer or service provider: 1. Remove the front mmWave radar, front bumper and front windshield. 2. Four wheels have been re-aligned due to wheel deviation; 3. A collision happens; 4. The ACC system performance degrades or the instrument panel cluster indicates a system abnormality.

### System descriptions Overview

Based on conventional cruise control, the adaptive cruise control (ACC) is designed to actively control the vehicle speed for auto follow-up while cruising. This is done via a front mmWave radar and a multi-purpose camera which detect the vehicle's distance and speed relative to the vehicle ahead. The ACC system can automatically switch between fixed-speed cruise and follow-up cruise depending on whether there is a vehicle ahead.

The intelligent cruise control (ICC) incorporates adaptive cruise control (ACC) and lane centering control (LCC). It provides the driver with longitudinal and lateral auxiliary control within the speed range of 0 to 125 km/h, reduces the driving burden of the driver and provides a safe and comfortable driving environment.

The predictive collision warning (PCW) system and autonomous emergency braking (AEB) system use the front mmWave radar and multi-purpose camera to detect vehicles and pedestrians ahead. Once a collision risk is detected, the system emits audible and visual alarms to urge the driver to take avoidance measures, while also increasing the potential braking pressure to provide sufficient reaction time for the driver. If the system determines that the possibility of collision continues to increase, it automatically engages the brake to assist the driver in avoiding or mitigating the collision impact.

The Front Cross Traffic Alert/Brake (FCTA/ FCTB) detects vehicles crossing in front of the vehicle through front mmWave radars on the left and right sides of the vehicle's front bumper to remind the driver and automatically brake the vehicle if necessary. When the vehicle is running at a low speed and FCTA/FCTB detects that there is a risk of collision with the front crossing vehicle, the system will remind the driver in visual and audible form. When a collision is about to occur, the vehicle will stop automatically to avoid collision.

The high beam assist (HMA) judges the current driving environment through a multipurpose camera sensor, and automatically activates or deactivates the high beam within the speed range of 35 to 145 km/h.

The lane departure warning (LDW) system detects lane lines ahead through a multipurpose camera. When the vehicle speed is 60 to 150 km/h and the driver unintentionally drifts out of the lane, the LDW system will warn the driver by steering wheel vibration, audible alarm and/or instrument display. The lane departure prevention (LDP) system detects lane lines ahead through a multi-purpose camera. When the vehicle speed is 60 to 150 km/h and the driver unintentionally drifts out of the lane towards the line, the LDP system activates and turns the steering wheel gently by providing reverse torque through the electric power steering (EPS) system, to prevent the vehicle from moving out of its lane. When the LDP system is activated, an alarm will be given at the same time to prompt the driver to take over the steering wheel to control the steering. The alarm lasts until the LDP deactivates and can be given in an acoustic or optical manner and through steering wheel vibration. If the system is activated twice or more within a continuous period of 180 seconds and the driver does not turn the steering wheel during activation, the system will send an alarm in the second activation or any further intervention. From the third intervention (and subsequent interventions), the alarm duration will be at leas 15 seconds longer than that of the previous alarm.

### System descriptions Overview

The emergency lane keeping assist (ELKA) system detects the lane lines ahead through a multi-purpose camera and detects the vehicles on the adjacent lane approaching from behind through a rear corner front mmWave radar. It works at vehicle speeds of 60 to 150 km/h when the driver unconsciously deviates from the lane or begins to change lanes. If another vehicle in an adjacent lane enters into a blind spot from the rear, and the system judges that it poses a collision risk, it will activate and control the electronic steering system (EPS) to provide reverse torque, keeping the vehicle in the current lane.

The blind spot assist system includes blind spot detection (BSD), lane change warning (LCW), rear cross traffic alert (RCTA), rear cross traffic brake (RCTB), rear collision warning (RCW) and door open warning (DOW). The system detects the environment behind the vehicle through rear corner mmWave radars on the left and right sides of the vehicle's rear bumper, to timely remind the driver to drive carefully and pay attention to driving safety.

The traffic sign recognition (TSR) system recognizes speed limit signs through the multipurpose camera. It displays relevant speed limit signs of the current road on the instrument and sends alarms when the vehicle speed exceeds the detected speed limit.

The intelligent speed limit control (ISLC) system incorporates the adaptive cruise control (ACC) and traffic sign recognition (TSR) functions. After the system is activated, when a speed limit sign is identified and the vehicle is speeding, the system will issue a prompt to ask whether to adjust the ACC cruise speed to the recognized speed limit value. After receiving confirmation from the driver, the system will automatically set the ACC cruise speed to the recognized speed limit value, so that the vehicle will not overspeed.

### Configuration writing

1. Conditions for re-calibrating the radar angle: replace with a new one.
2. Configuration writing steps: a. Connect the VDS and enter the diagnostic system interface.

![](images/9439238c1569d9fa86f97dff181f95497fb7d3e935ff5dc9235cd4b20f702fda.webp)

b. Enter the ACC interface. c. Tap to calibrate. d. Select the configuration corresponding to the vehicle model to perform configuration writing. 3. Conditions for re-calibrating radar angle: a. The existing one is replaced with a new one. b. The radar is removed or installed. c. The radar position changes during maintenance. d. The system prompts that the radar angle deviation is too large.

4. Necessary equipment:

a. VDS b. ACC/MPC static calibration service tool c. Adjusting bolt (model: 3.5 mm hexagonal socket head cap bolt) 5. Description of ACC mid-range radar adjusting bolt: a. The upper right bolt is used to adjust the horizontal angle.

b. The lower left bolt is used to adjust the vertical angle.

Calibration process of ACC mid-range radar

1. Preparation for calibration:

a. Four-wheel alignment should be completed for the vehicle.
b. The calibration site for placing equipment and parking vehicles must be flat.
c. The vehicle suspension and steering system are in normal condition without damage.
d. The windshield washer fluid, coolant and brake fluid are filled up.
e. The tire pressure is normal.
f. The vehicle is unloaded.
g. The spare tire and on-board tools are installed in place.

2. Calibration process:

a. After the vehicle is parked, pull up the handbrake, center the steering wheel, power on the vehicle, and move the equipment to the front of the vehicle. b. Fix four disc assemblies on four tires by using three high-strength magnets to attach them on the brake disc and installing the two discs with scales on two rear wheels. Point the laser scale at the rear wheels with the display screen facing upward, and press and hold to start the power supply. Slightly adjust the angle so that laser beams illuminate on the scales of rear discs. At this time, slightly adjust the steering wheel left and right to make the readings of the positions illuminated by two laser beams the same so as to ensure that the wheels are completely aligned (the laser scale is in power-saving mode. It will automatically power off if it is not operated for a period of time and can be woken up by pressing the switch again).

c. Install the laser scales on the 2 front wheel discs in a reverse direction to make them face the calibration tooling, adjust the angle so that the laser beam irradiates horizontally on the ranging plate center marking line of the cross beam of the

calibration tool. At this time, observe the distance values displayed on the 2 laser scales, and twist to adjust the base of the calibration tool to make the distance values on laser scales consistent and meet the calibration requirements. Then move the base left and right to make the pointer indication value of ranging plate on the cross beam scale consistent. At this time, determine the position of calibration tool. Rotate 4 adjusting legs clockwise to contact the ground and fix the position.

### Configuration writing

d. Press the up and down buttons on the manual controller to change the value on the display screen to "18.6". At this time, observe that the horizontal bubble behind the reflection board reaches the center position, and the reflection board is vertical to the ground.

e. Turn the battery and switch behind the reflection board to "ON" position, so that a laser beam can be emitted from the center of the front of the reflection board. Take out the label at the front radar of the vehicle. Rotate the hand wheel at the top of the equipment, adjust the height of laser beam to make it irradiate in the center of ACC radar. At this time, the calibration tool is completely positioned.

f. Turn on the ACC radar, connect the VDS, enter the diagnostic system interface, select the calibration procedure and operate according to the instructions on the VDS: Step 1: When VDS prompts that the reflection board is in position 1, press the up and down buttons of the manual controller within 20 seconds to change its displayed value to 18.1, and the actual corresponding angle of the reflection board is -2 Step 2: When VDS prompts that the reflection board is in position 2, press the up and down buttons of the manual controller within 20 seconds to change its displayed value to 19.2, and the actual angle of the corresponding reflection board is +2 Step 3: When VDS prompts that the reflection board is in position 3, press the up and down buttons of the manual controller within 20 seconds to change its displayed value to 18.6, and the actual

corresponding angle of the reflection board is 0.

![](images/b4b4d46007952706c9a4397257b42b145fe57484388c4048ebcc2379502c4f8d.webp)

g. After operation, VDS will automatically display whether the radar needs to be calibrated and display specific information for calibration. After calibration as required, use the VDS to test once again. If the diagnosis result shows that the number of turns to be adjusted is 0 and no calibration is needed, the calibration is successful. (The number of turns to be adjusted can be ignored if it is 2.5 turns).

Multi-purpose camera (MPC)

### Configuration writing

1. Conditions for re-writing the model configuration: replace with a new one.
2. Configuration writing steps: a. Connect the VDS and enter the diagnostic system interface. b. Enter the multi-purpose camera interface.
c. Tap to calibrate.

![](images/167757352a158b4503a98fc08bd40ff6970f49c1c2a397c13d01d8949f337917.webp)

d. Select the configuration corresponding to the vehicle model to perform configuration writing.

3. Conditions for re-calibration:

a. The sample is replaced with a new one. b. The multi-purpose camera assembly is removed or installed. c. The front windshield is replaced.

Calibration process of multipurpose camera (MPC)

1. Preparation for calibration:

a. Four-wheel alignment should be completed for the vehicle.
b. The calibration site for placing equipment and parking vehicles must be flat.
c. The illumination of the calibration plate must be uniform during calibration.
d. The tire pressure is normal.
e. The vehicle is unloaded.
f. The headlight must be turned off.
g. The vehicle speed is 0, and the vehicle is powered on.
h. There is no obstruction between the calibration plate and camera.

Calibration process:

1. Preparation for calibration:

a. Four-wheel alignment should be completed for the vehicle.
b. The calibration site for placing equipment and parking vehicles must be flat.
c. The illumination of the calibration plate must be uniform during calibration.
d. The tire pressure is normal.
e. The vehicle is unloaded.
f. The headlight must be turned off.
g. The vehicle speed is 0, and the vehicle is powered on.
h. There is no obstruction between the calibration plate and camera.

2. Calibration process:

a. After the vehicle is parked, pull up the handbrake, center the steering wheel, power on the vehicle, and move the equipment to the front of the vehicle. b. Fix four disc assemblies on four tires by using three highstrength magnets to attach them on the brake disc and installing the two discs with scales on two rear wheels. Point the laser scale at the rear wheels with the display screen facing upward, and press and hold to start the power supply. Slightly adjust the angle so that laser beams illuminate on the scales of rear discs. At this time, slightly adjust the steering wheel left and right to make the readings of the positions illuminated by two laser beams the same so as to ensure that the wheels are completely aligned (the laser scale in power -saving mode. It will automatically power off if it is not operated for a period of time and can be woken up by pressing the switch again). c. Install the laser laser scales scales on the 2 front wheel discs in a reverse direction to make them face the calibration tooling, adjust the angle so that the laser beam irradiates horizontally on the ranging plate center marking line of the cross beam of the calibration tool. At this time, observe the distance values displayed on the 2 laser scales, and twist to adjust the base of the calibration tool to make the distance values on laser scales consistent and meet the calibration requirements. Then move the base left and right to make the pointer indication value of ranging plate on the cross beam scale consistent. At this time, determine the position of calibration tool. Rotate 4 adjusting legs clockwise to contact the ground and fix the position. d. Loosen the 3 handles fixing the scale behind the pillar to allow the scale the fall

### Configuration writing

to the ground and tighten the handles. At this time, the value indicated by the pointer is the actual distance from the black and white pattern center of calibration plate to the ground. e. Rotate the lifting device handle on the pillar, and move the MPC2 calibration

plate assembly to a height that meets the calibration requirements (the center of camera calibration plate shall be at the same height as the camera) according to the indicated value of the pointer behind the pillar. At this time, the position of the equipment and the vehicle has been determined.

f. Use VDS to enter the multipurpose camera interface, click the calibration option and operate according to the instructions on the computer until the computer prompts that the calibration is successful.

3. Calibration process:

a. After the vehicle is parked, pull up the handbrake, center the steering wheel, power on the vehicle, and move the equipment to the front of the vehicle.

b. Fix four disc assemblies on four tires by using three high-strength magnets to attach them on the brake disc and installing the two discs with scales on two rear wheels. Point the laser scale at the rear wheels with the display screen facing upward, and press and hold to start the power supply. Slightly adjust the angle so that laser beams illuminate on the scales of rear discs. At this time, slightly adjust the steering wheel left and right to make the readings of the positions illuminated by two laser beams the same so as to ensure that the wheels are completely aligned (the laser scale is in power-saving mode. It will automatically power off if it is not operated for a period of time and can be woken up by pressing the switch again).

c. Install the laser scales on the 2 front wheel discs in a reverse direction to make them face the calibration tooling, adjust the angle so that the laser beam irradiates horizontally on the ranging plate center marking line of the cross beam of the calibration tool. At this time, observe the distance values displayed on the 2 laser scales, and twist to adjust the base of the calibration tool to make the distance values on laser scales consistent and meet the calibration requirements. Then

move the base left and right to make the pointer indication value of ranging plate on the cross beam scale consistent. At this time, determine the position of calibration tool. Rotate 4 adjusting legs clockwise to contact the ground and fix the position.

d. Loosen the 3 handles fixing the scale behind the pillar to allow the scale the fall to the ground and tighten the handles. At this time, the value indicated by the pointer is the actual distance from the black and white pattern center of calibration plate to the ground.

e. Rotate the lifting device handle on the pillar, and move the MPC2 calibration plate assembly to a height that meets the calibration requirements (the center of camera calibration plate shall be at the same height as the camera) according to the indicated value of the pointer behind the pillar. At this time, the position of the equipment and the vehicle has been determined.

### Configuration writing

f. Use VDS to enter the multipurpose camera interface, click the calibration option and operate according to the instructions on the computer until the computer prompts that the calibration is successful.

Slope calibration and initialization is required in the case of ECU replacement, and only initialization is required in other cases.
The calibration can be completed when the system is faulty and the power is turned on the horizontal road.

![](images/afb74e945ba6fb6db00f2007bab0ea1d31a9c3d758973673bd9683a6ee02fdf9.webp)

4. Double click "Element Action Test 1" on the left side.
5. Double click "Slope Calibration".
6. A prompt of successful calibration shall be displayed in the lower right corner; otherwise, re-calibration is required.
7. Double click "Element Action Test 2" on the left side.
8. A prompt of successful calibration shall be displayed in the lower right corner; otherwise, re-calibration is required.

### System descriptions Overview

The infotainment system includes 4G network, PAD unit, Bluetooth phone, smart voice recognition, vehicleinfotainment interaction, on-board radio, USB, SD card assembly, audio and video equipment interface, image system and other functions.

Main components:

USB interface assembly It includes 2 USB interfaces, of which only 1 USB interface supports audio and video file reading, and both USB interfaces can be used for charging handheld devices.

4G/WIFI/BT/GPS antenna

It supports 4G internet access and Wi-Fi connection to phones, among other functions.

EDR camera

Loop recording: When the memory card space is insufficient, the recorder will automatically overwrite the oldest videos to enable continuous loop recording. Emergency recording: In the event of a collision or scratch, pressing the emergency button will automatically lock the video recorded 4 to 7 minutes prior to the accident, preventing it from being overwritten. Collision recording: Once the recorder is activated and in recording mode, it will automatically enable collision detection. In the event of a severe accident, the recorder will automatically save an important segment of the recorded video capturing the accident. This specific recording will not be overwritten or deleted.

Panoramic camera

It includes two main functions: 2D panoramic view and transparent panoramic view. In R gear, these functions will be triggered automatically. Users can also activate and enable these functions manually by pressing the hard button on the steering wheel or the APP soft button on the touchscreen homepage. The image is input through 720P high-definition cameras and transmitted through the LVDS interface at a rate of 30 frames per second.

Rearview camera

It is mainly used to provide the user with a reversing image during reversing, to help the user complete parking faster. The user can use this function by turning on APP button on the touchscreen homepage if necessary or by shifting into R gear.

Multi-purpose camera assembly

It can assist the radar in identifying stationary vehicles ahead and remind the driver of active deceleration at a suitable distance, so as to avoid collision with such vehicles. The multi-purpose camera can assist the radar in identifying the vehicle ahead which runs inside the current lane and has a

coincident trajectory with the current vehicle as the target, and allow the driver to follow the target in cruise control mode.
The multi-purpose camera and the radar can timely identify the vehicles which run on both sides and try to change to the current lane as targets, and allow the driver to brake when necessary.
The multi-purpose camera and radar can identify pedestrians ahead in time, so that the vehicle can completely avoid possible accidents.

### Engine sound simulator system Systems Manual

Overview

The acoustic vehicle alerting system(AVAS) issues an acoustic warning to the pedestrians near the vehicle during driving at a low speed.

When the vehicle is driven forward:

if 0km/h ﹤ V≤20km/h, the acoustic warning will become louder with the increase of the speed.

if 20km/h ﹤ V≤30km/h, the acoustic warning will become weaker with the increase of the speed.

When the vehicle speed V is > 30km/h, the prompt sound stops automatically.

When driving in reverse gear

A continuous uniform acoustic wanning will be issued.

### Exterior Light System Exterior lighting system

Systems Manual

System Overview

The lighting system provides lighting for driving at night. The exterior lighting mainly includes head lights, stop lights, license plate lights. Each light is installed at its required position and provided with respective control switch, circuit, fuse and so forth, thereby forming the lighting system. The lighting system also serves for signaling, with such optical signals as steering signal, brake signal, hazard warning signal, outline marker signal, and reversing signal generated to warn other drivers and pedestrians for the purpose of driving safety.

In addition to the traditional lighting, the auto light and head light delayed shut-off makes the use of light more convenient and user-friendly.

Automatic light

Turn the light switch group to AUTO. The light switch group will determine the state according to the external light intensity collected by the four-in-one sensor to automatically control the on and off conditions of light, and turn on the side light or head light according to the light intensity.

Head light delayed shut-off

When the head lights are turned ON and the vehicle is powered OFF, the head lights will not go out immediately. The light switch group will time to turn off the head light after 10 s.

### Inspection and adjustment of headlight dimming function

It is essential to adjust the headlight cluster assembly in case of lighting deviation or replacement. Preparation of test screen

![](images/6121a4bb065c7e0748d581dc648a9d5ad8ab6437383c9141a466a0c8b1f7932b.webp)

1. Use a 1.2 m (height) × 2 m (width) wall or whiteboard to make the test screen. Draw a longitudinal centerline (corresponding to the vehicle) and dimming test paper position boxes on the wall or whiteboard.

![](images/db2e59d83afac4364a2f7f884147e862a1546586f60dc75468e663c4b7280986.webp)

2. The requirements for dimensions of the centerline and dimming test paper position boxes are as follows:

Designation of letters in the figure:

![](images/4183e781dac2bac0d389c50380b5b6394ecf1734ea31af7f58a06658152de45e.webp)

Preparation of dimming test paper

? Reminder:

To download the dimming test paper, please refer to attachments of Dolphin dimming position diagrams in the TSB (EM2E Dimming Position Diagram - Left and EM2E Dimming Position Diagram - Right).

1. Print the test paper for Dolphin model on an A2 (420 mm × 594 mm) paper in a professional print shop.

![](images/ef1b675707c2bafdb90b11c3e74bac7b63511664961604c09c8b5bbdf3f2b046.webp)

2. Cut the printed test paper along the dotted line and laminate it.

? Reminder:

The methods for the left and right sides are the same. Take the left one as an example. Make sure that the test paper is printed at 1:1 scale, with the dotted line box for left or right headlight cluster being i Reminder: 430 mm × 350 mm. Please check that dimensions are correct after printing. Attach the test paper to the corresponding position box of the test screen. After use, put it in a folder or file bag, and properly keep it in the spare parts warehouse.

### Preparation of test site

1. Make sure that the test site is flat and spacious, and avoid the influence of strong light irradiation on dimming.

![](images/65bb250b80f86ff7c4f03c42b22420ec73e3fa9de4aa42a1ed7edd89b9f933a0.webp)

2. Draw a straight line parallel to the test screen on the ground 3 m away from the test screen, draw the vehicle centerline on the ground, and make sure that the centerline is perpendicular to the 3 m line and the test screen.

Designation of letters in the figure:

![](images/26b9327bfa574011bca77d90d8b6d5ad33f718cd98dc963e643c6e3ef7ba73fb.webp)

### Preparation of test vehicle

1. Check and make sure that there is no damage or deformation of the vehicle and around the headlights.

2. Make sure that the vehicle lubricating oil level and the coolant level meet the design requirements.

3. Make sure that the tire pressure meets the standard inflation pressure requirement.

4. Never place other articles in the vehicle, but be sure to place the tools delivered with the vehicle at the specified positions.

5. Have a person weighing 75 kg seated in the driver's seat (counterweight method is allowed if the weight is below 75 kg).

6. Place the vehicle on a horizontal plane and shake the vehicle body from side to side to make the chassis suspension of the vehicle stay in a stable state.

7. For a vehicle equipped with a dimmer switch, turn the headlight adjustment switch to "0" position before dimming; for a vehicle without a dimmer switch (i.e. automatic dimming), check whether the light MIL on the instrument panel cluster illuminates before dimming. If it illuminates or flashes, conduct repair, make a record and provide feedback; if it does not illuminate or flash, complete initialization with the VDS.

![](images/8c133cb2c3fcf4fcd13442e885e9441b533208c99398bd8a7335bc92009802bd.webp)

8. Connect the VDS and enter the diagnostic system interface.

9. Power on the vehicle.

10. Go to: Model diagnosis/(corresponding model code)/Body module/Headlight adjustment unit/Headlight initialization.

Test steps

### Reminder:

– For a model with joint adjustment of high and low beams, only low beams need to be adjusted. There are two light patterns of low beams, namely " and " ". The lower inflection point of cut-off line is taken as the light pattern center of low beams, while the brightest spot is taken as the light pattern center of high beams.
– If low beams need to be shielded for adjusting high beams, headlight surfaces cannot be directly shielded or the shielding time cannot exceed 2 minutes as headlight covers are made of plastic, so as to avoid gathering of heat that may cause burn-out of headlight covers.
– During light adjustment, observe beam positions while rotating the adjusting bolt. Make proper adjustment at one time whenever possible. Refrain from continuous and prolonged rotation of the adjusting bolt with an electric screwdriver to prevent need for subsequent readjustment caused by excessive adjustment.
– point to the test box center whenever possible.

Adjust the light inflection

1. Attach the dimming test paper of the corresponding model to the position box (for a wall, it is recommended to use a paper

tape; for a whiteboard, it is recommended to use a magnet).

2. Park the vehicle in front of the 3 m line, that is, the low beam reference center (the intersection point between the low beam bulb axis and the light cover) is 3 m away from the test screen. In addition, keep the vehicle centerline overlap with the vehicle centerline drawn on the ground and be vertically aligned with the centerline on the test wall.

3. Start the vehicle and turn on headlights.

4. Check whether the light pattern centers of headlights are in the corresponding test boxes. If so, headlights are normal. If not, adjust headlights.

![](images/0214fc3a122c9a57c1e267fb0f0cd8b274ec23a3274f1cf2420769a457a1bcb8.webp)

5. Adjust the headlight cluster assembly.

i Reminder:

The adjustment method of left headlight cluster assembly is the same as the right one. Take the left one as an example.

a. Adjust the light source in horizontal direction. b. Adjust the light source in vertical direction.

### Reminder:

Light sources mentioned above refer to irradiation sources of headlight cluster assemblies.

> ⚠️ **Внимание:** 
> Ensure that the environment is well ventilated when recycling or filling refrigerant. It may cause suffocation.

### A Warning:

The maintenance of A/C system must be carried out by professional and technical personnel, who must wear goggles during the maintenance. Avoid contact of the refrigerant and refrigerant oil with the eyes and skin. In case of contact with eyes, rinse immediately with clean water; In case of skin contact and frostbite, rinse with water and apply Vaseline ointment to the skin. If the situation is serious, seek medical attention as soon as possible.

### A Caution:

Because the refrigeration oil has strong water absorption, when removing the
system pipeline or the pipeline connection of the components, it is necessary to seal the pipeline and component connection interfaces immediately to prevent moisture and sundries from entering the interior.
When inspecting and cleaning the dirt or debris on the condenser radiator fin, do not use a high pressure water gun to flush it, as this may damage the radiator fin. It can be brushed with a soft brush.
When the total amount of the refrigeration oil of A/C system is as low as 80 ml
due to the leakage, excessive wear of the compressor may occur.
Avoid overfilling the refrigerant, otherwise the cooling effect may be poor.
When recovering refrigerant, do not
open the valve too much, otherwise the refrigerant will be discharged too quickly and the refrigeration oil in the system may also be brought out quickly.

### Systems Manual

![](images/2b4cd1616afac96cd7e52812f6c4409b153ce35f72a286c55276a986c40869ce.webp)
Component Position Diagram

![](images/1c0df24aea0d5f368193d4360b85d39775cdc769d40d2032109f4495b577e886.webp)

System Function Principle

System overview

This vehicle is equipped with a self-regulating A/C system designed with the single evaporator and applied to Deluxe and Premium SUVs. The system is mainly composed of compressor, condenser, HVAC assembly, cooling pipe, air duct and A/C control module, with the cooling, heating, defrosting & defogging and ventilation functions. The system uses the low pressure PTC air heater for heating, and the vapor compression refrigeration cycle for cooling. The refrigerant used is R134a. The system is controlled by pressing the A/C button. The mode, cooling and heating and internal/external circulation throttles of the automatic A/C body are controlled by motors.

### Principles of cooling system

The scroll compressor used for this model extracts the gaseous refrigerant from the evaporator and presses it into the condenser. The high-pressure gaseous refrigerant is liquefied through the condenser for heat exchange (heat release), and the heat is taken away by the exterior air. The highpressure liquid refrigerant is depressurized by the throttling effect of the expansion valve, the low-pressure liquid refrigerant is vaporized in the evaporator for heat exchange (heat absorption), and the cooled air near the evaporator is blown into the compartment by the blower. The gaseous refrigerant is pumped away by the compressor and pumped into the condenser, therefore, the refrigerant flows circularly in an enclosed space, and the heat in the compartment is continuously discharged to the outside, so that the temperature in the compartment is reduced to a suitable level.

Gas expands and temperature decreases:

![](images/f4a613f659ec126911a2300219a7354b0a2ed45dc6e6174b5d06e44a9808ab2b.webp)

Absorption of heat from the environment

![](images/2cecb73264b9f4e9944a87b5671acb86aecbf95b19a5ce4a28cd4a5ef1a9f4be.webp)

Principles of heating system

The heating system adopts heat pump or air PTC for heating. The heating system is mainly composed of PTC, compressor, gas-liquid separator, integrated thermal management module, heat exchanger, blower, air duct and control mechanism. The enclosure of the heating fan unit is integrated with that of the evaporator. The blower and air duct are shared with the refrigeration system.

When the compressor is working, the high temperature and high pressure gaseous refrigerant discharged from the compressor discharge pipe enters the indoor condenser through the heating hard pipe. And the air blown by the blower distributes the heat flow of the high temperature and high pressure refrigerant to the passenger compartment or the front glass to raise the cabin temperature and defrost. The low temperature and low pressure liquid refrigerant dissipated in the indoor condenser becomes gaseous after the heat is absorbed from the environment by the integrated thermal management module (or the electric coolant of the motor) The refrigerant then passes through the gas-liquid separator and enters the compressor, and so on, to achieve warm air heating.

Compressed gas and temperature rise

![](images/c0337e0ce733b4fa9504b292e4850c56c66e7471e45639de8887cebd53133410.webp)

Heat dissipation into the cabin

![](images/25c8acbc233b492b1b8d6d3e02f1a79b063e09151e2481969f280c308ec9d0a2.webp)

Battery thermal management function

Battery thermal management function includes battery cooling, battery heating and battery recirculation functions. It is the main function of heat pump air conditioning system.

The characteristics of the heat pump A/C system include direct cooling and direct heating of the battery; Non-extremely low temperature, reducing A/C energy consumption; Extremely low temperature environment, supplemented by motor reactive power and low voltage PTC low efficient heat generation. Common functions include: heat pump heating, A/C cooling, battery cooling, battery heating, synchronous start-up of cooling and battery cooling synchronous start-up of heating and battery heating, dehumidification and other working modes.

### ? Warning:

Care should be taken for the A/C system repair and the precautions for the A/C system repair should be followed, as detailed Common Sense of Safety. Failure to observe these instructions may result in serious personal injury or damage to vehicle components. – Be sure to read the refrigerant recovery and filling machine's instruction manual carefully and strictly follow its instructions.

Recover the Refrigerant

1. Start the A/C and set it up as follows.

HVAC switch: turned on Temperature setting: Lo Blower speed: Gear 7 Running time: more than 3 min

0 Reminder:

The above settings can concentrate most of the refrigeration oil in the A/C system into the compressor, and try to avoid the discharge of refrigeration oil. If the A/C does not work due to a compressor failure, the preceding settings are not required.

2. Switch the power supply to OFF position and ensure that the A/C system does not work (for example, the compressor and electronic fan do not work).

3. Take out the high pressure bonnet and low pressure bonnet from the A/C pipeline in the front compartment.

![](images/738a3993fa92101870b2438758d790bd9a64571af178021a3263d54372bc73c8.webp)

4. Use a refrigerant recovery and filling machine to connect the A/C system pipeline. a. Connect the refrigerant recovery and filling machine high pressure quick connector to the A/C system high pressure connector. b. Connect the low-pressure quick connector of the refrigerant recovery and filling machine to the low-pressure connector of the A/C system.

5. Slowly open the pressure valves on the high and low pressure sides of the refrigerant recovery and filling machine, while avoiding over-opening the valves, and continue to operate according to the instructions of the refrigerant recovery and filling machine to recover the refrigerant.

### A Caution:

Observe and record the liquid level of the refrigeration oil bottle on the refrigerant recovery and filling machine before and after the refrigerant recovery, and calculate and record the difference.

6. Remove the connection between the refrigerant recovery and filling machine and the vehicle in reverse order.

### A Caution:

The high pressure bonnet and low pressure bonnet must be installed to avoid contamination of the joint by impurities.

### ? Warning:

Do not turn on the A/C switch before filling the A/C system with refrigerant, otherwise the compressor may work without refrigerant, resulting in compressor damage.

> ⚠️ **Внимание:** 
> Make sure that the A/C system is free of refrigerant and then vacuumize. If you are unable to confirm the presence of refrigerant in the A/C system, please follow the "refrigerant recovery" procedure described above.
>
> ![](images/fc1170ddced280cc0df3995f132626e83311df597c7ed09a7c7d9858cc062db6.webp)
>
> 1. Use a refrigerant recovery and filling machine to connect the A/C system pipeline. a. Connect the refrigerant recovery and filling machine high pressure quick connector to the A/C system high pressure connector. b. Connect the low-pressure quick connector of the refrigerant recovery and filling machine to the low-pressure connector of the A/C system.
>
> 2. Turn on the pressure valve on the high pressure and low pressure sides of the refrigerant recovery and filling machine, and continue to operate according to the operating instructions of the
>
> refrigerant recovery and filling machine to evacuate.
>
> 3. At the end of the vacuum, maintain the pressure for 5 min and check for any pressure change.
>
> If the pressure does not change, continue to add refrigeration oil or refrigerant; If the pressure increases, it indicates that the cooling system leaks, the leakage fault must be eliminated before supplementing refrigeration oil or refrigerant.
>
> 4. After vacuuming, if you need to replenish refrigeration oil, please continue to perform the following process of "filling refrigeration oil".
>
> 5. Continue with the following process of "filling refrigerant".
>
> Fill the Refrigerant Oil

### A Caution:

– Before filling the refrigerant, it is necessary to confirm the A/C system must be filled with
refrigeration oil: according to the discharge amount of recycling refrigerant (observe and
record the refrigerant recovery and filling machine refrigeration oil bottle level, before and after
the refrigerant recovery is discharge amount), A/C some refrigeration oil (if replaced), or in the case of refrigerant leakage, the total refrigeration oil to be filled. The filling refrigeration oil must be carried out according to the above-mentioned value of calculation.

### A Caution:

Must use refrigeration oil that pass the requirements and asks, otherwise the A/C system may be damaged.

1. Calculate the discharge amount A of the refrigeration oil during refrigerant recovery = refrigerated oil level after refrigerant recovery - refrigerated oil level before refrigerant recovery.

2. According to the replacement of A/C system parts, or refrigerant leakage, choose the corresponding refrigeration oil replenishment B:

![](images/1ed3ccfe003e849a3ea420072c6e87fa3112663a8121cf4cf950e6f0b3c03bbe.webp)

3. Calculate the total amount of refrigeration oil to be filled C=A+B.

4. Use the refrigerant recovery and filling machine, and fill the refrigeration oil according to its instructions.

Refrigeration oil model: POE-68. Refrigeration oil filling quantity: C (add according to the above computation)

5. Continue with the following process of "filling refrigerant".

Add the Refrigerant

### Reminder:

When using a refrigerant recovery device, make sure that the refrigerant is sufficient for filling of the system. The refrigerant recovery device cannot recover 100% of the refrigerant in the A/C system.

### ? Warning:

Never use refrigerant of different models, and only the refrigerant of the applicable model can be used. Serious system failures may occur if the refrigerant is mixed or misused.

1. Before filling the refrigerant, extract the vacuum of the A/C pipeline with a refrigerant recovery and filling machine for 15 min.

2. Use the refrigerant recovery and filling machine, and fill the refrigerant according to its instructions.

Refrigerant model: R134a

Refrigerant filling quantity: 900± 10g

3. Close the pressure valve on the high pressure and low pressure sides of the refrigerant recovery and filling machine after filling.
4. Remove the high and low pressure end quick connectors from the refrigerant recovery and filling machine.
5. Install the high pressure bonnet and low pressure bonnet.
6. Turn on the A/C and check whether the A/C system is operating normally (such as smooth operation without abnormal sound, normal cooling and heating functions, etc.).

### ? Caution:

After removing pipeline connections, properly seal all pipe fittings as soon as possible to prevent dust, impurities, and foreign objects from entering the A/C system and causing system faults.

1. Recycle the refrigerant. Refer to Refrigerant recovery and filling

2. Power off the low-voltage electrical system. Refer to Power-off and power-on of lowvoltage electrical system

4. Remove the instrument panel upper body assembly. Refer to Removal and installation of instrument panel upper body assembly

6. Remove the instrument panel lower body assembly. Refer to Removal and installation of instrument panel lower body assembly

10. Lift the front end of the carpet on the front passenger's seat side.

11. Lift the round sound insulation cotton.

![](images/418a33f5f39e52d149058fbff31e5d497d696fc47224179003170a98be40739e.webp)

Removal and installation of thermal management integrated module
Removal

### A Caution:

After removing pipeline connections, properly seal all pipe fittings as soon as possible to prevent dust, impurities, and foreign objects from entering the A/C system and causing system faults.

1. Recycle the refrigerant. Refer to Refrigerant Recovery and Refueling

2. Power off the low-voltage electrical system. Refer to Power-off and Power-on of Low Voltage Electrical System

3. Power off the high-voltage electrical system. Refer to Power-off and power-on of highvoltage electrical system

4. Remove the front gutter channel assembly. Refer to Removal and installation of front gutter channel assembly

5. Remove the fuse box bracket I. Refer to Installation and Removal of Power Distribution Box Bracket

### A Caution:

The harness through hole rubber sleeve must be installed reliably. Under normal use, the rubber sleeve will not be separated from the installation position.

Connectors must be reliably connected and in good contact.
According to the actual installation position
of the harness on the vehicle, in order to
avoid the harness sag and displacement.
The harness must be fixed in accordance
with the predetermined arrangement.
– After installation, it must have a reasonable
clearance with the surrounding parts to
prevent abrasion. Do not touch the sharp edge of the body
directly, and leave a gap to prevent the
harness from being worn and causing
malfunction. During assembly, do not pull the harness
too tight, so as to prevent the vehicle
from driving on the bumpy road, and
the displacement of vehicle parts will
become large, thus lengthening the
harness, causing false connection of
internal connection points of the harness,
or even breaking the harness.
After installation, ensure that it will not be
pressed by other parts, and will not be collided by other parts and their fastener.
Avoid grounding faults caused by crushing,
abrasion or rupture of harness insulation. Do not contact the connector directly with rainwater and oil.

### System descriptions Overview

Vehicle wiring harnesses run through the whole vehicle and connect all electrical equipment. They can transmit both current and signal, playing an important role in vehicle circuits.

Main components:

Electric wire: It is the main part of the wiring harness, usually called conductor. It is the main body of the wiring harness and mainly used to carry the current required by the load. Connector: It is an indispensable component for connecting the wiring harness with other electrical equipment, which can be divided into a wiring harness end connector and an electrical appliance end connector. Wiring harness wrapping: It is mainly used to protect the wiring harness. The application conditions and methods on the wiring harness assembly vary with the wrapping material. The wrapping should be selected based on the specific service environment, wear resistance and heat resistance of the wiring harness.

Wiring harness fixture: As a flexible part, the wiring harness cannot be arranged according to the set position. Therefore, it is necessary to constrain its layout path and use additional parts to fix it. These parts are called wiring harness fixtures, mainly including tie wraps, clips, rubber sheaths and wiring harness brackets. Depending on the different installation environment of wiring harness, such as installation space, temperature and waterproof requirements, the shape and material of each wiring harness fixture are also different.

Wiring harness accessories: such as product labels on the wiring harness assembly.

### A Caution:

– When installing the tailgate harness I, use a wire rope to connect one end of the harness firmly, the wire rope from the harness mounting hole and out of the other mounting hole. In the process of pulling the wire rope, pull it slowly. If it is stuck, do not use brute force to pull it hard. To prevent damage to the harness, pull it back a distance until one end of the harness is pulled out of the mounting hole.

1. Install in the reverse order of removal.

Installation

1. Install it in the reverse order of removal.

### Removal and installation of battery pack GND wiring harness Removal

1. Power off the low-voltage electrical system. Refer to Power-off and power-on of lowvoltage electrical system

![](images/3b47e6ae0e5de070967c646eccabbfa6eac293e56b66a39be869f2c6b612fb40.webp)

2. Remove the battery pack GND wiring harness.

a. Remove fixing bolt. Tightening torque: 22±2 N•m

b. Remove 1 fixing bolt and take out the battery pack GND wiring harness. Tightening torque: 18±2 N•m

Installation

1. Install it in the reverse order of removal.

### Removal and installation of 12 V battery negative wiring harness Removal

1. Remove the carpet support bracket. Refer to

2. Power off the low-voltage electrical system. Refer to Power-off and power-on of lowvoltage electrical system

![](images/f4bffa3df1136b2fedcf0be879e7345434e98a5db00fb457ecdec1beaba671c4.webp)

Installation

3. Remove the 12 V battery negative wiring harness.

a. Remove 1 fixing bolt. Tightening torque: 9± N•m
b. Remove 1 fixing bolt and take out the 12 V battery negative wiring harness. Tightening torque: 22±2 N•m

1. Install it in the reverse order of removal.

### Panel Installation and Removal of Shift Control Mechanism Panel Assembly Removal

A Caution:

Be careful when removing the trim panel to avoid scratching the surface material.

1. Power off the low voltage electrical system. See Power-off and Power-on of Low Voltage Electrical System

![](images/0a1ed1e9524f1ab0a06790a9d1eb613662afee07c50e4f6afbe46e4e6e1066f6.webp)

2. Carefully pry out the shift control mechanism panel assembly.

![](images/bc7245410c4dbd9efc74e3f76696140261213b50d2e0d27382fba347b117cfb4.webp)

3. Disconnect connector, and take out the shift control mechanism panel assembly.
